tsa-a20-v01.quick_english: There — the initiation for perfection of refinement for the knowledge-fit, and the with-seed release-initiation for those incapable of that: once it is performed, the guru should teach the lifelong remaining course.

tsa-a20-v02.quick_english: There the remaining course is threefold — daily, occasional, desired-for. The last belongs to the practitioner alone; it is not decided here.

tsa-a20-v03.quick_english: There the regularly occurring is the daily; identity-with-that alone is the occasional; serving it are twilight worship, daily practice, festival day, sacred thread, and the rest.

tsa-a20-v04.quick_english: That too is daily, by fixedness of its own time — say some.

tsa-a20-v05.quick_english: But the occasional, even for those abiding in his teaching, is irregular — namely the coming of guru and his circle, their festival day, knowledge-gaining day, and the rest — say some.

tsa-a20-v06.quick_english: There fixed worship, twilight worship, guru worship, festival worship, sacred thread — thus unfailing.

tsa-a20-v07.quick_english: Occasional are gaining knowledge, gaining scripture, the coming to the guru's circle's house, their birth-refinement-going days, worldly festival, scripture exposition, beginning-middle-end, seeing deities, gathering, dream command, gaining rule-expiation — this occasional is the cause of special worship.

tsa-a20-v08.quick_english: There the disciple's chief mantra — with power, whose essence is consciousness-flash, unwritten — one should transmit by mouth-lineage alone. Then, to perfect identity-with-that, the disciple should practice identity at the twilights; through that, at all times, to perfect such refinement-gain; and daily one should worship the Supreme Lord on altar or liṅga.

tsa-a20-v09.quick_english: There, on a heart-pleasing altar, meditated as a stainless mirror — having seen one's very form, non-different from the worshippable deity-wheel, as it were body-reflected — one should worship with heart-pleasing flowers, scents, wine, libations, food, smoke, lamps, gifts, praise, song, music, dance and the rest; murmur; praise — to obtain doubt-free identity-with-that.

tsa-a20-v10.quick_english: For in a mirror, one gazing ceaselessly at one's own face — certainty of its nature swiftly comes about. And here no order is chief — apart from identity-with-that.

tsa-a20-v11.quick_english: Entered into identity with the supreme mantra, his beast-latency stain gone, his whole snare-net of bonds melted by devotion-taste penetration — whatever heart dwells in that is highest to be taken up, say our gurus.

tsa-a20-v12.quick_english: Having lain upon the flood of being, the ultimate-minded flashes forth light — which —

tsa-a20-v13.quick_english: supreme-nectar-vision-ness — by her they are worshipped, the secret-knowers.

tsa-a20-v14.quick_english: Having made the ground-bearing, sprinkled in the moment with wonder-taste — with taken, mentally, own-being flowers exuding own fragrance.

tsa-a20-v15.quick_english: From the course of the priceless cup of my bliss-nectar-full heart — you with the Goddess together, in the body-temple of God, I worship day and night.

tsa-a20-v16.quick_english: The sense stated in two verses contemplated within — one should contemplate the deity-wheel.

tsa-a20-v17.quick_english: Then showing seals, murmuring, offering of that.

tsa-a20-v18.quick_english: Dismissal through unity with the to-be-awakened.

tsa-a20-v19.quick_english: The chief food-offering one should eat oneself, or cast all into water — for the water-born living are previously initiated, through oblation-food — say the scripture-knowers.

tsa-a20-v20.quick_english: But in eating cats, mice, dogs and the rest, doubt is born — for hell. Even the knower, from wish to favor the world, should not do such; or, leaving the world, one should stay — thus is altar-sacrifice.

tsa-a20-v21.quick_english: Now on the liṅga: there one should not install the liṅga with secret mantras; especially the manifest — thus on previously installed ones, in invocation-dismissal order, one should do worship, as the support.

tsa-a20-v22.quick_english: There guru's body, own body, Śakti's body, secret-scripture book, hero's cup, rosary, weapon, arrow-thing, pearl, golden, made of flowers, scents, substances and dear things, mirror or as liṅga one should worship.

tsa-a20-v23.quick_english: There, by support-power alone comes ever-greater mantra-success — thus earlier and earlier is chief, since following the support's qualities; and of mantras, there in the to-be-won, each chief — say the scripture-gurus.

tsa-a20-v24.quick_english: Everywhere pride of non-difference from the Supreme Lord alone is the highest refinement.

tsa-a20-v26.quick_english: There general, general-general, general-special, special-general, special, special-special — thus sixfold festival, from completion of the rite.

tsa-a20-v28.quick_english: There in each month first and fifth days are general; fourth, eighth, ninth, fourteenth, fifteenth of both fortnights are general-general; on both of these too, in fitting planet-star conjunctions on each stated tithi, general-special. Mārgaśīrṣa's first night-quarter, on dark ninth; Pauṣa's midnight, on dark ninth; Māgha's midnight, on bright fifteenth; Phālguna's midday, on bright twelfth; Caitra's on bright thirteenth; Vaiśākha's on dark eighth; Jyaiṣṭha's on dark ninth; Āṣāḍha's on first day; Śrāvaṇa's day fore-part, on dark eleventh; Bhādrapada's midday, on bright sixth; Āśvayuja's bright-ninth day; Kārttika's first night-quarter, on bright ninth — thus special festival.

tsa-a20-v29.quick_english: Citrā-moon, Maghā-Jupiter, Tiṣya-moon, Pūrva-phalgunī-Mercury, Śravaṇa-Mercury, Śatabhiṣak-moon, Diti's two, Rohiṇī-Venus, Viśākhā-Jupiter, Śravaṇa-moon — thus.

tsa-a20-v30.quick_english: If in Mārgaśīrṣa-first order in due numbers it is, excluding Āśvayuja — then special-special.

tsa-a20-v31.quick_english: If another special is on another festival, then that is after-festival, they say.

tsa-a20-v32.quick_english: In star-planet conjunction, time is not chief.

tsa-a20-v33.quick_english: The tithi alone — from special gain; but continuity of after-rite time on festival day is chief. By after-rite primacy: of festival rites, after-rite is image-rite and wheel-rite — synonyms.

tsa-a20-v34.quick_english: There the guru, his circle with offspring, knower of truth, maiden, outcast woman, courtesan, bleeding woman, truth-knowing woman or — in wheel-rite the chief to be worshipped, especially collectively.

tsa-a20-v35.quick_english: There in the middle the guru, in his covering-order — from guru to the bound ones, hero and power in order — thus in wheel or row formation one should sit. Then with scents, smoke, flowers and the rest in order one should worship. Then, having contemplated the vessel as Sadāśiva-formed, having filled with wine meditated as Śakti-nectar, there having worshipped the enjoyer-power as Śiva, having thereby sated the deity-wheel, having contemplated the triad-meeting of man, power, and Śiva in nature, in covering-descent order — primacy of release and enjoyment, outside and inside — one should do sating; then in re-circulation order — thus the complete circling nourishes the wheel.

tsa-a20-v36.quick_english: There, having placed the universe-made vessel on the base, having sated the deity-wheel, one should sate oneself with the saluted. If no vessel — auspicious folded shell-hands; or with the right hand vessel-shaped — auspicious — with two, right laid above, made jointless, folded shell-hands; with falling drops vetālas and guhyakas are pleased, by the flow Bhairava. Here entry is to be given to no one; if by mistake one entered, one should make no doubt; having made, again double wheel-rite one should do. Then fried foods, meals and the rest before, as desired, should be scattered — in a hidden house or, without code-names, by the word deity one should join all — thus is hero-mixture rite.

tsa-a20-v37.quick_english: Then at the end with gifts, betel, clothes and the rest one should sate — thus this most excellent image-rite.

tsa-a20-v38.quick_english: Even unseen-maṇḍala, by image-rite worshipping festival days, within a year alone gains the fruit stated for putrakas — without twilight practices and the rest. Thus for the old, enjoyers, women is this rule — when power descends, to be taught by the guru.

tsa-a20-v40.quick_english: And it in Ratnamālā, Triśiromata, Siddhāmata and the rest is preceded by rule and fulfills the Lord's command — and this is said in the Tantrāloka: without the sacred thread, all is fruitless — thus.

tsa-a20-v41.quick_english: There from bright Āṣāḍha up to Kula-full-moon day-end the sacred thread is to be done; there Kārttika dark fifteenth fulfills Kula-wheel and daily-wheel — say the Nitya-tantra knowers.

tsa-a20-v42.quick_english: Māgha bright fifteenth — say the Bhairavakulormi knowers.

tsa-a20-v43.quick_english: Southern-course-end fifteenth — say the Tantrasadbhāva knowers.

tsa-a20-v44.quick_english: There according to means, having worshipped the God, having sated with oblation, one should give the sacred thread — one should make from gold-pearl-jewel-made beginning up to cloth-thread-cotton-kuśa-wombed even.

tsa-a20-v45.quick_english: And that with tattva-number knots, and with pada-kalā-bhuvana-varṇa-mantra-number knots — one knee-ending, another navel-ending, another throat-ending, another on the head — thus four sacred threads to the God and to the guru, by contemplating all-paths-full forms, one should give; to the rest one — thus.

tsa-a20-v46.quick_english: Then great festival is to be held — four-month, seven-day, three-day — thus chief and fallback courses. When means exist, monthly the sacred thread; or in four months; or once. In not doing it, one should murmur expiation. Even the knower, even with means, in not doing incurs; in greed-covered knowledge non-doing, from disgrace of knowledge.

tsa-a20-v47.quick_english: When, even having attained wisdom, the Lord's teaching is defiled — then needing expiation.

tsa-a20-v50.quick_english: At knowledge-gaining and the rest, at worldly festival's end too — everywhere excess of consciousness-blaze, nearness of the deity-wheel especially comes about — thus by considering such excess, just such distinction, in after-rite and the rest, one should do.

tsa-a20-v52.quick_english: One should request the guru complete in all scriptures for exposition — he too, to own disciple or even another's, should expound scripture fit for fit refinement; even to one abiding in lower teaching, from compassion, his heart stirred by hope of power-descent born of the Lord's varied will, one should expound — excluding secret teaching.

tsa-a20-v53.quick_english: There, exposition made for the devoted seated low, of restrained speech-mind-body, becomes fruitful. First, on ground smeared with perfumes and the rest, having drawn or resolved — lotus-base, four-cornered, lotus-triad, in lotus-middle Vāgīśī, on left and right Gaṇapati and guru — one should worship; on the base-lotus, the exposition-worthy wish-deity.

tsa-a20-v54.quick_english: Then, having sated the wheel with the common offering-vessel rite, one should expound — sūtra-sentence-chapter text, uncontradicted before and after, making first the position rightly joined, rightly refuting, proving the provandum, showing the drift, one should expound to chapter's end, no more; even there, at each section's end, sating and worship — until exposition's close.

tsa-a20-v55.quick_english: Then too, having worshipped, having dismissed the knowledge-seat, having smeared, one should cast it in the deep.

tsa-a20-v58.quick_english: Though even the truth-knowing-established needs no expiation and the rest, yet to favor those who share release through conduct alone, one should show the conduct-course.

tsa-a20-v59.quick_english: But the truth-unknowing, whose enjoyment-release hangs on conduct alone — if the rule is crossed, not doing expiation, becomes a raw-flesh eater for a hundred years, thus the expiation rule is to be stated. There in woman-slaying there is no expiation; elsewhere, having known strength-weakness, unbroken Goddess Mālinī from one time beginning up to three hundred thousand one should repeat, until doubt falls away. At its end special worship; even there wheel-rite — for it everywhere is remaining.

tsa-a20-v62.quick_english: At all rites' ends, the rite gathered in, next day one should do guru-worship — for before, as rite-limb he is pleased, not chiefly — thus doing it chiefly, not doing, by office-bond one is bound.

tsa-a20-v63.quick_english: Thus it in every way one should do.

tsa-a20-v64.quick_english: There, having drawn a svāstika maṇḍala, there having given a golden seat, there having worshipped the entire path-course, having installed that seat by that, to him having done worship, sating, meal, gift, self — thus having offered, the food-leavings having begged, having bowed, oneself having tasted, one should do wheel-worship.

tsa-a20-v01.speaker: Teacher (śeṣavartana charter)
tsa-a20-v01.question: What follows initiation?
premises: yā dīkṣā saṃskārasiddhyai jñānayogyān prati — initiation for refinement-perfection, for the knowledge-fit.
yā ca tadaśaktān prati mokṣadīkṣā sabījā — and with-seed release-initiation for the incapable.
tasyāṃ kṛtāyām ājīvaṃ śeṣavartanaṃ guruḥ upadiśet — once performed, the guru teaches the lifelong remainder.
tsa-a20-v01.inference: Charter: two initiations (knowledge-fit vs incapable) → lifelong course taught by guru.

tsa-a20-v02.speaker: Teacher (threefold remainder)
tsa-a20-v02.question: How is the remainder divided?
premises: tatra nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyam iti trividhaṃ śeṣavartanam — daily, occasional, desired-for.
antyaṃ ca sādhakasyaiva — the last for the practitioner alone.
tat na iha niścetavyam — not decided here.
tsa-a20-v02.inference: Threefold remainder; desired-for rite deferred (practitioner-only, out of scope).

tsa-a20-v03.speaker: Teacher (daily vs occasional)
tsa-a20-v03.question: What is daily, what occasional?
premises: tatra niyatabhavaṃ nityaṃ — the regularly occurring is daily.
tanmayībhāva eva naimittikaṃ — identity-with-that alone is occasional.
tadupayogi saṃdhyopāsanaṃ pratyaham anuṣṭhānaṃ parvadinaṃ pavitrakam ityādi — serving it: twilight worship, daily practice, festival day, sacred thread.
tsa-a20-v03.inference: Daily = recurrent; occasional = identity; servants listed.

tsa-a20-v04.speaker: Some (ke-cit view)
tsa-a20-v04.question: Is even that daily?
premises: tad api nityaṃ svakālanaiyatyāt — that too is daily, by fixedness of its own time.
iti kecit — say some.
tsa-a20-v04.inference: Minority view: fixed-time occasional counts as daily.

tsa-a20-v05.speaker: Some (occasional irregularity)
tsa-a20-v05.question: When is the occasional irregular?
premises: naimittikaṃ tu tacchāsanasthānām api aniyatam — occasional even for his abiders is irregular.
tadyathā gurutadvargāgamanaṃ tatparvadinaṃ jñānalābhadinam ityādikam — e.g. guru's circle coming, their festival, knowledge-day.
iti kecit.
tsa-a20-v05.inference: Occasion list; irregularity even for insiders.

tsa-a20-v06.speaker: Teacher (unfailing set)
tsa-a20-v06.question: What never lapses?
premises: tatra niyatapūjā saṃdhyopāsā gurupūjā parvapūjā pavitrakam iti avaśyaṃbhāvi — fixed, twilight, guru, festival worship, sacred thread: unfailing.

tsa-a20-v07.speaker: Teacher (occasion catalogue)
tsa-a20-v07.question: What triggers special worship?
premises: naimittikam jñānalābhaḥ śāstralābho ... samayaniṣkṛtilābhaḥ — knowledge-gain through rule-expiation-gain.
ity etat naimittikaṃ viśeṣārcanakāraṇam — this occasional causes special worship.
tsa-a20-v07.inference: Twelve occasions catalogued; special worship their fruit.

tsa-a20-v08.speaker: Teacher (mantra transmission)
tsa-a20-v08.question: How is the chief mantra given?
premises: kṛtadīkṣākasya śiṣyasya pradhānaṃ mantraṃ savīryakaṃ saṃvittisphuraṇasāram alikhitaṃ vaktrāgamenaiva arpayet — unwritten, power-holding mantra transmitted by mouth-lineage alone.
tanmayībhāvasiddhyarthaṃ ... saṃdhyāsu tanmayībhāvābhyāsaṃ kuryāt — practice identity at twilights.
taddvāreṇa sarvakālaṃ ... pratyahaṃ ca parameśvaraṃ ca sthaṇḍile vā liṅge vā abhyarcayet — through that, always; daily worship the Lord on altar or liṅga.
tsa-a20-v08.inference: Unwritten mouth-transmission; twilight identity-practice; daily altar/liṅga worship.

tsa-a20-v09.speaker: Teacher (mirror rite)
tsa-a20-v09.question: How is identity contemplated?
premises: hṛdye sthaṇḍile vimalamakuravad dhyāte — on the heart-altar meditated as stainless mirror.
svam eva rūpaṃ yājyadevatācakrābhinnaṃ mūrtibimbitam iva dṛṣṭvā — seeing own form non-different from the deity-wheel, body-reflected.
hṛdyapuṣpagandhāsavatarpaṇanaivedyadhūpadīpopahārastutigītavādyanṛttādinā pūjayet japet stuvīta — worship with the full offering train; murmur; praise.
tanmayībhāvam aśaṅkitaṃ labdhum — to gain doubt-free identity.
tsa-a20-v09.inference: Mirror-contemplation of own form as deity-wheel; full offerings; doubt-free identity.

tsa-a20-v10.speaker: Teacher (mirror reason)
tsa-a20-v10.question: Why does the mirror work?
premises: ādarśe hi svamukham aviratam avalokayataḥ tatsvarūpaniścitiḥ acireṇaiva bhavet — ceaseless mirror-gazing swiftly certifies own form.
na cātra kaścit kramaḥ pradhānam ṛte tanmayībhāvāt — no order here is chief apart from identity.
tsa-a20-v10.inference: Swiftness without order; identity alone chief.

tsa-a20-v11.speaker: Our gurus (heart doctrine)
tsa-a20-v11.question: What is to be taken up?
premises: paramantrat...raśajālasya — entered into supreme-mantra identity, stain gone, bond-net melted.
yad adhivasati hṛdayaṃ tad eva paramam upādeyam — whatever heart dwells in that is highest to take up.
iti asmadguravaḥ — say our gurus.
tsa-a20-v11.inference: Guru saying: the indwelling heart is the highest take-up.

tsa-a20-v12.speaker: Verse (flash)
tsa-a20-v12.question: What flashes?
premises: adhiśayya pāramārthikaḥ bhāvaprasaraṃ prakāśam ullasati — lying upon, the ultimate-minded flashes forth the flood of being as light.
yā — which.

tsa-a20-v13.speaker: Verse (secret worship)
tsa-a20-v13.question: Who is worshipped?
premises: paramāmṛtadṛktvaṃ tayārcayante rahasyavidaḥ — by her, supreme-nectar-visioned, secret-knowers are worshipped.
tsa-a20-v13.inference: Inversion: knowers worshipped by her vision.

tsa-a20-v14.speaker: Stotra verse (ground rite)
tsa-a20-v14.question: How is the ground made?
premises: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām — the ground-bearer sprinkled in wonder-taste's moment.
āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ — with taken mental own-being flowers exuding own fragrance.
uncertainties: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ junction obscure; rite-sense from stotra frame.

tsa-a20-v15.speaker: Stotra verse (day-night worship)
tsa-a20-v15.question: What is the worship?
premises: ānandāmṛtanirbharasvahṛdayānarghārghapātrakramāt — from the priceless cup of my bliss-nectar-full heart.
tvāṃ devyā saha dehadevasadane devārcaye 'harniśam — you with the Goddess, in the body-temple, I worship day and night.

tsa-a20-v16.speaker: Teacher (seal)
tsa-a20-v16.question: What follows the verses?
premises: iti ślokadvayoktam artham antar bhāvayan devatacakraṃ bhāvayet — contemplating within the two-verse sense, contemplate the deity-wheel.

tsa-a20-v17.speaker: Teacher (closing acts)
tsa-a20-v17.question: What closes worship?
premises: tato mudrāpradarśanaṃ japaḥ tannivedanam — then seal-showing, murmuring, offering of that.

tsa-a20-v18.speaker: Teacher (dismissal)
tsa-a20-v18.question: How dismiss?
premises: bodhyaikātmyena visarjanam — dismissal through unity with the to-be-awakened.
tsa-a20-v18.inference: Dismissal by unity, not sending away.

tsa-a20-v19.speaker: Scripture-knowers (remains)
tsa-a20-v19.question: What of the food-offering?
premises: mukhyaṃ naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyāt sarvaṃ vā jale kṣipet — eat the chief offering, or cast all in water.
jalajā hi prāṇinaḥ pūrvadīkṣitāḥ carubhojanadvāreṇa — for water-born beings are previously initiated, through oblation-food.
iti āgamavidaḥ.
tsa-a20-v19.inference: Eat or water-cast; water-beings already initiated.

tsa-a20-v20.speaker: Teacher (limit)
tsa-a20-v20.question: What is forbidden?
premises: mārjāramūṣakaśvādibhakṣaṇe tu śaṅkā janitā nirayāya — eating cats, mice, dogs: doubt born, for hell.
jñānī api lokānugrahecchayā na tādṛk kuryāt — even the knower, to favor the world, should not.
lokaṃ vā parityajya āsīta — or leave the world and stay.
iti sthaṇḍilayāgaḥ — thus altar-rite.
tsa-a20-v20.inference: Impure eating barred even for knowers; withdrawal alternative; altar-rite sealed.

tsa-a20-v21.speaker: Teacher (liṅga rule)
tsa-a20-v21.question: How worship the liṅga?
premises: atha liṅge tatra na rahasyamantraiḥ liṅgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet — with secret mantras install no liṅga.
viśeṣāt vyaktam — especially the manifest.
pūrvapratiṣṭhiteṣu āvāhanavisarjanakrameṇa pūjāṃ kuryāt ādhāratayā — on installed ones, invocation-dismissal worship, as support.
tsa-a20-v21.inference: No secret-mantra installation; manifest preferred; installed ones worshipped in order.

tsa-a20-v22.speaker: Teacher (liṅga substitutes)
tsa-a20-v22.question: What can serve as liṅga?
premises: tatra guruḥ svadehaḥ ... śaktidehe rahasyaśāstrapustakaṃ vīrapātram akṣasūtraṃ prāharaṇaṃ bāṇīyaṃ mauktikaṃ sauvarṇaṃ ... makuraṃ vā liṅgam arcayet — guru's body through mirror: any may be worshipped as liṅga.
tsa-a20-v22.inference: Fourteen substitutes catalogued; any worshippable as liṅga.
uncertainties: bāṇīyaṃ formation obscure; missile-sense from weapon series. makuraṃ sense uncertain; reflective object in series.

tsa-a20-v23.speaker: Scripture-gurus (support doctrine)
tsa-a20-v23.question: Why does support matter?
premises: tatra ca ādhārabalād eva adhikādhikamantrasiddhiḥ bhavati — by support-power alone ever-greater mantra-success.
pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ pradhānam ādhāraguṇānuvidhāyitvāt — earlier ever chief, following the support's qualities.
tatra tatra sādhye tattatpradhānam — in each goal, each chief.
iti śāstraguravaḥ.
tsa-a20-v23.inference: Support-power scales success; earlier supports chief.

tsa-a20-v24.speaker: Teacher (highest refinement)
tsa-a20-v24.question: What is highest?
premises: sarvatra parameśvarābhedābhimāna eva paramaḥ saṃskāraḥ — everywhere, pride of non-difference from the Lord alone is highest refinement.

tsa-a20-v25.speaker: Teacher (next topic)
tsa-a20-v25.question: What next?
premises: atha parvavidhiḥ — now the festival rule.

tsa-a20-v26.speaker: Teacher (six parvan)
tsa-a20-v26.question: How is festival sixfold?
premises: tatra sāmānyaṃ sāmānyasāmānyaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣo viśeṣasāmānyaṃ viśeṣo viśeṣaviśeṣaś ca iti ṣoḍhā parva — six.
pūraṇāt vidheḥ — from completion of rite.
tsa-a20-v26.inference: Six festival grades; parvan = rite-completion celebrated.

tsa-a20-v27.speaker: Teacher (definition)
tsa-a20-v27.question: Why parvan?
premises: pūraṇāt vidheḥ — from completion of the rite.

tsa-a20-v28.speaker: Teacher (calendar)
tsa-a20-v28.question: Which days?
premises: māsi māsi prathamaṃ pañcamaṃ dinaṃ sāmānyaṃ — monthly 1st, 5th: general.
caturthāṣṭamanavamacaturdaśapañcadaśāni dvayor api pakṣayoḥ sāmānyasāmānyam — 4/8/9/14/15 both fortnights: general-general.
anayor ubhayor api rāśyoḥ ... sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ — with fitting planet-star conjunctions: general-special.
mārgaśīrṣasya prathamarātribhāgaḥ kṛṣṇanavamyām ... kārttikasya prathamo rātribhāgaḥ śuklanavamyām iti viśeṣaparva — twelve month-places: special festival.
tsa-a20-v28.inference: Full festival calendar: monthly + fortnightly + conjunctional + twelve specials.

tsa-a20-v29.speaker: Teacher (conjunctions)
tsa-a20-v29.question: Which conjunctions?
premises: citrācandrau maghājīvau ... śravaṇacandrau iti — ten star-planet pairs.
uncertainties: dityau dual obscure; star-pair sense from list.

tsa-a20-v30.speaker: Teacher (special-special)
tsa-a20-v30.question: When special-special?
premises: yadi mārgaśīrṣādikrameṇa yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bhavati āśvayujaṃ varjayitvā tadā viśeṣaviśeṣaḥ — Mārgaśīrṣa-first due order minus Āśvayuja: special-special.

tsa-a20-v31.speaker: They say (anuparvan)
tsa-a20-v31.question: What is anuparvan?
premises: anyaviśeṣaś ced anyaparvaṇi tadā tad anuparva ity āhuḥ — another special on another festival: after-festival, they say.

tsa-a20-v32.speaker: Teacher (time rule)
tsa-a20-v32.question: Does time rule?
premises: bhagrahayoge ca na velā pradhānam — in star-planet conjunction, time is not chief.

tsa-a20-v33.speaker: Teacher (rite synonyms)
tsa-a20-v33.question: What are the festival rites?
premises: tither eva viśeṣalābhāt — the tithi alone, from special gain.
anuyāgakālānuvṛttis tu parvadine mukhyā — after-rite continuity on festival day is chief.
anuyāgaprādhānyāt parvayāgānām anuyāgo mūrtiyāgaḥ cakrayāgaḥ iti paryāyāḥ — by after-rite primacy: after-rite, image-rite, wheel-rite are synonyms.

tsa-a20-v34.speaker: Teacher (wheel company)
tsa-a20-v34.question: Who is worshipped in the wheel?
premises: tatra guruḥ tadvargyaḥ sasaṃtānaḥ tattvavit kanyā antyā veśyā aruṇā tattvavedinī vā — guru through truth-knowing woman.
cakrayāge mukhyapūjyāḥ viśeṣāt sāmastyena — in wheel-rite chief worship, especially collectively.

tsa-a20-v35.speaker: Teacher (wheel order)
tsa-a20-v35.question: How is the wheel rite done?
premises: tatra madhye guruḥ ... iti krameṇa ... āsīta — guru center, covering-order, wheel or row.
gandhadhūpapuṣpādibhiḥ krameṇa pūjayet — worship in order.
pātraṃ sadāśivarūpaṃ dhyātvā ... pūrayitvā — vessel as Sadāśiva, filled with Śakti-nectar wine.
bhoktrīṃ śaktiṃ śivatayā pūjayitvā ... devatācakratarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā — enjoyer-power as Śiva; deity-wheel sated.
naraśaktiśivātmakatritayamelakaṃ dhyātvā — triad-meeting meditated.
āvaraṇāvataraṇakrameṇa mokṣabhogaprādhānyaṃ bahir antaś ca tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt — covering-descent order, release-enjoyment primacy, outside and inside.
punaḥ pratisaṃcaraṇakrameṇa evaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇaṃ cakraṃ puṣṇāti — re-circulation completes the circling.
tsa-a20-v35.inference: Seating, worship, vessel-filling, enjoyer-as-Śiva, triad, descent, inside-outside, re-circulation — the full wheel course.

tsa-a20-v36.speaker: Teacher (vessel rite)
tsa-a20-v36.question: How without a vessel, and how guarded?
premises: tatrādhāre viśvamayaṃ pātraṃ sthāpayitvā ... svātmānaṃ vanditena tena tarpayet — place universe-vessel, sate wheel, sate self with it.
pātrābhāve bhadraṃ vellitaśuktiḥ — without vessel: folded shell-hands.
dakṣahastena pātrākāraṃ ... niḥsaṃdhīkṛtābhyāṃ — right hand vessel-shaped over left, jointless.
patadbhir bindubhir vetālaguhyakāḥ saṃtuṣyanti dhārayā bhairavaḥ — drops please vetālas; flow, Bhairava.
atra praveśo na kasyacid deyaḥ — no entry to anyone.
pramādāt praviṣṭasya vicāraṃ na kuryāt — of mistaken entrant make no doubt.
kṛtvā punar dviguṇaṃ cakrayāgaṃ kuryāt — instead do double wheel-rite.
tato 'vadaṃśān ... vikīryeta ... devatāśabdena sarvān yojayet — scatter foods; in hidden house, join all by deity-name.
iti vīrasaṃkarayāgaḥ — thus hero-mixture rite.
tsa-a20-v36.inference: Hand-vessel substitute; drop/flow pleasures; no-entry rule with double-rite remedy; deity-name union.

option_choices.reason: hands context (dakṣahastena, dvābhyām) decisive; literal shell possible

tsa-a20-v37.speaker: Teacher (close)
tsa-a20-v37.question: How close the wheel rite?
premises: tato 'nte dakṣiṇātāmbūlavastrādibhis tarpayet — at end sate with gifts, betel, clothes.
iti pradhānatamo 'yaṃ mūrtiyāgaḥ — thus this most excellent image-rite.

tsa-a20-v38.speaker: Teacher (concession)
tsa-a20-v38.question: Who may use image-rite?
premises: adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'pi mūrtiyāgena parvadināni pūjayan varṣād eva putrakoktaṃ phalam eti — even unseen-maṇḍala, by image-rite on festival days, gains putraka-fruit within a year.
vinā saṃdhyānuṣṭhānādibhiḥ — without twilight practices.
vṛddhānāṃ bhogināṃ strīṇāṃ vidhir ayam śaktipāte sati upadeṣṭavyo guruṇā — for old, enjoyers, women, when power descends, the guru teaches it.
tsa-a20-v38.inference: Concession rite for old/enjoyers/women with śaktipāta; putraka-fruit within a year.

tsa-a20-v39.speaker: Teacher (next topic)
tsa-a20-v39.question: What next?
premises: atha pavitrakavidhiḥ — now the sacred-thread rule.

tsa-a20-v40.speaker: Teacher (pavitraka warrant)
tsa-a20-v40.question: On what authority?
premises: sa ca ... vidhipūrvakaḥ pārameśvarājñāpūrakaś — preceded by rule, fulfilling the Lord's command.
uktaṃ caitat śrītantrāloke — said in the Tantrāloka.
vinā pavitrakeṇa sarvaṃ niṣphalam — without the thread, all fruitless.
Ratnamālā, Triśiromata, Siddhāmata cited.
tsa-a20-v40.inference: Rule-precedent + Lord's command + Tantrāloka seal: thread indispensable.

tsa-a20-v41.speaker: Nitya-tantra knowers (season)
tsa-a20-v41.question: When the thread?
premises: tatra āṣāḍhaśuklāt kulapūrṇimādināntaṃ kāryaṃ pavitrakam — from bright Āṣāḍha to Kula-full-moon end.
kārttikakṛṣṇapañcadaśī kulacakraṃ nityacakraṃ pūrayati — Kārttika dark fifteenth fulfills both wheels.
iti śrīnityātantravidaḥ.
tsa-a20-v41.inference: Āṣāḍha-to-Māgha season; Kārttika dark-fifteenth double fulfillment.

tsa-a20-v42.speaker: Bhairavakulormi knowers (date)
tsa-a20-v42.question: When?
premises: māghaśuklapañcadaśī iti śrībhairavakulormividaḥ — Māgha bright fifteenth.

tsa-a20-v43.speaker: Tantrasadbhāva knowers (date)
tsa-a20-v43.question: When?
premises: dakṣiṇāyanāntapañcadaśī iti śrītantrasadbhāvavidaḥ — southern-course-end fifteenth.

tsa-a20-v44.speaker: Teacher (thread making)
tsa-a20-v44.question: How make and give?
premises: tatra vibhavena devaṃ pūjayitvā āhutyā tarpayitvā pavitrakaṃ dadyāt — per means worship, oblate, give.
sauvarṇamuktāratnaviracitāt prabhṛti paṭasūtrakārpāsakuśagarbhāntam api kuryāt — from gold-jewel-made down to cloth-thread-cotton-kuśa, make.

tsa-a20-v45.speaker: Teacher (thread sizes)
tsa-a20-v45.question: How many, what size?
premises: tac ca tattvasaṃkhyagranthikaṃ padakalābhuvanavarṇamantrasaṃkhyagranthi ca — tattva-number knots and adhva-number knots.
jānvantam ekaṃ nābhyantam aparaṃ kaṇṭhāntam anyat śirasi anyat — knee, navel, throat, head: four.
devāya ... gurave ca ... dadyāt — to God and guru.
śeṣebhya ekam — one to the rest.
samastādhvaparipūrṇatadrūpabhāvanena — contemplating all-paths-full forms.
tsa-a20-v45.inference: Four threads (body-lengths) + one for rest; knot-counts = adhva numbers.

tsa-a20-v46.speaker: Teacher (festival and lapse)
tsa-a20-v46.question: What festival, what if lapsed?
premises: tato mahotsavaḥ kāryaḥ cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ ca — great festival; four-month rite, seven or three days.
mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ — chief and fallback courses.
sati vibhave māsi māsi pavitrakam atha vā caturṣu māseṣu atha vā sakṛt — monthly, or four-monthly, or once.
tadakaraṇe prāyaścittaṃ japet — if not done, murmur expiation.
jñānī api sambhavadvitto 'pi akaraṇe pratyavaiti — even the knowing with means incurs by not doing.
lobhopahitajñānākaraṇe jñānanindāpatteḥ — from greed-covered non-doing, disgrace of knowledge.
tsa-a20-v46.inference: Festival courses; lapse = japa; means-withholding = knowledge-disgrace.
uncertainties: mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ formation obscure; chief-fallback sense from context. sambhavadvitto formation obscure; means-sense from context.

tsa-a20-v47.speaker: Verse (expiation)
tsa-a20-v47.question: When expiation?
premises: yadā prāpyāpi vijñānaṃ dūṣitaṃ parameśaśāsanaṃ tadā prāyaścittī — when attained wisdom defiles the Lord's teaching, needing expiation.
tsa-a20-v47.inference: Defiled teaching after attainment = expiation case.

tsa-a20-v48.speaker: Citation (seal)
tsa-a20-v48.question: By what word?
premises: iti vacanāt — thus by the statement.

tsa-a20-v49.speaker: Teacher (section seal)
tsa-a20-v49.question: What was this?
premises: ity eṣa pavitrakavidhiḥ — thus this is sacred-thread rule.

tsa-a20-v50.speaker: Teacher (excess)
tsa-a20-v50.question: What of festival excess?
premises: jñānalābhādau laukikotsavānte 'pi sarvatra saṃvidullāsādhikyaṃ devatācakrasaṃnidhiḥ viśeṣato bhavati — at knowledge-gain through worldly festival's end, consciousness-blaze excess and deity-wheel nearness especially.
tathāvidhādhikyaparyālocanayā tathāvidham eva viśeṣam anuyāgādau kuryāt — considering such excess, do just such distinction in after-rite and the rest.
tsa-a20-v50.inference: Excess-blaze calls for matching distinction in after-rites.

tsa-a20-v51.speaker: Teacher (next topic)
tsa-a20-v51.question: What next?
premises: atha vyākhyāvidhiḥ — now exposition rule.

tsa-a20-v52.speaker: Teacher (who expounds)
tsa-a20-v52.question: Who may expound, to whom?
premises: sarvaśāstrasampūrṇaṃ guruṃ vyākhyārtham abhyarthayeta — request the all-scripture-complete guru for exposition.
so 'pi svaśiṣyāya paraśiṣyāyāpi vā ... vyākcakṣīta — he expounds to own or another's disciple, fit text for fit refinement.
adharaśāsanasthāyāpi karuṇāvaśāt — even to lower-teaching abiders, from compassion.
īśvarecchāvaicitryodbhāvitaśaktipātasambhāvanābhāvitahṛdayo vyākcakṣīta — heart stirred by hope of power-descent, expound.
marmopadeśavarjam — excluding secret teaching.
tsa-a20-v52.inference: Expound to fit disciples, even lower ones from compassion, on śaktipāta-hope; secrets excluded.

tsa-a20-v53.speaker: Teacher (exposition setup)
tsa-a20-v53.question: How prepare exposition?
premises: tatra nimnāsanasthitebhyaḥ tadparebhyo niyamitavāṅmanaḥkāyebhyo vyākhyā kriyamāṇā phalavatī bhavati — for low-seated devoted restrained ones, exposition bears fruit.
prathamaṃ gandhādiliptāyāṃ bhuvi ullikhya saṃkalpya vā — first on perfumed ground, drawn or resolved.
padmādhāraṃ caturaśraṃ padmatrayaṃ padmamadhye vāgīśīṃ vāmadakṣiṇayoḥ gaṇapatigurū ca pūjayet — lotus-base, square, triad, Vāgīśī center, Gaṇapati-guru flanks.
ādhārapadme vyākhyeyakalpadevatām — on base-lotus the wish-deity of exposition.
tsa-a20-v53.inference: Low seats, perfumed ground, lotus-maṇḍala with Vāgīśī center.

tsa-a20-v54.speaker: Teacher (exposition method)
tsa-a20-v54.question: How expound?
premises: tataḥ sāmānyārghapātrayogena cakraṃ tarpayet — first sate the wheel with common vessel.
tato vyākcakṣīta sūtravākyapaṭalagrantham pūrvāparāviruddhaṃ — expound sūtra-text uncontradicted.
tantrāvṛttiprasaṅgasamuccayavikalpādiśāstranyāyaucityena — by scriptural reasoning.
pūrvaṃ pakṣaṃ samyak ghaṭayitvā samyak ca dūṣayan — first join the position rightly, refute rightly.
sādhyaṃ sādhayan tātparyavṛttiṃ pradarśayan — prove the provandum, show the drift.
paṭalāntaṃ vyākcakṣīta nādhikam — to chapter's end, no more.
tatrāpi vastvante vastvante tarpaṇaṃ pūjanam — at each section's end sating and worship.
yāvad vyākhyāsamāptiḥ — until exposition's close.

tsa-a20-v55.speaker: Teacher (dismissal)
tsa-a20-v55.question: How close?
premises: tato 'pi pūjayitvā vidyāpīṭhaṃ visṛjya upalipya agādhe tat kṣepet — worshipped, dismissed the knowledge-seat, smeared, cast it in the deep.

tsa-a20-v56.speaker: Teacher (section seal)
tsa-a20-v56.question: What was this?
premises: ity vyākhyāvidhiḥ — thus exposition rule.

tsa-a20-v57.speaker: Teacher (next topic)
tsa-a20-v57.question: What next?
premises: atha samayaniṣkṛtiḥ — now rule-expiation.

tsa-a20-v58.speaker: Teacher (who needs)
tsa-a20-v58.question: Who needs expiation?
premises: yady api tattvajñānaniṣṭhasya prāyaścittādi na kiṃcit — for the truth-established, no expiation at all.
tathāpi caryāmātrād eva mokṣabhāginaḥ tān anugrahītum ācāravartanīṃ darśayet — yet to favor release-sharers through conduct alone, show the conduct-course.
tsa-a20-v58.inference: Established need none; conduct-sharers get the course shown.

tsa-a20-v59.speaker: Teacher (breach)
tsa-a20-v59.question: What if the rule is crossed?
premises: atattvajñānī tu caryaikāyattabhogamokṣaḥ ... bhavatīti — the truth-unknowing becomes a raw-flesh eater for a hundred years.
iti prāyaścittavidhiḥ vaktavyaḥ — so the expiation rule is to be stated.
tatra strīvadhe prāyaścittaṃ na asti — in woman-slaying, no expiation.
anyatra tu balābalaṃ jñātvā ... mālinīṃ ... trilakṣāntam āvartayet — elsewhere, knowing strength, repeat Mālinī to three hundred thousand.
yāvat śaṅkāvicyutiḥ bhavati — until doubt falls.
tadante viśeṣapūjā tatrāpi cakrayāgaḥ sa hi sarvatra śeṣabhūtaḥ — then special worship; even there wheel-rite, everywhere remaining.
tsa-a20-v59.inference: Woman-slaying inexpiable; Mālinī-repetition to doubt's fall; wheel-rite everywhere remaining.

option_choices.reason: āvartayet repeat governs texts; trilakṣa count selects mantra-reading

tsa-a20-v60.speaker: Teacher (section seal)
tsa-a20-v60.question: What was this?
premises: ity samayaniṣkṛtividhiḥ — thus rule-expiation rule.

tsa-a20-v61.speaker: Teacher (next topic)
tsa-a20-v61.question: What next?
premises: atha gurupūjāvidhiḥ — now guru-worship rule.

tsa-a20-v62.speaker: Teacher (guru-worship)
tsa-a20-v62.question: When and how worship the guru?
premises: sarvayāgānteṣu upasaṃhṛte yāge aparedyuḥ gurupūjāṃ kuryāt — at all rites' ends, next day do guru-worship.
pūrvaṃ hi sa vidhyaṅgatayā toṣito na tu prādhānyena — before pleased as rite-limb, not chiefly.
tāṃ prādhānyena akurvan adhikārabandhena baddho bhavati — not doing it chiefly, bound by office-bond.
tsa-a20-v62.inference: Next-day chief worship; limb-only before; omission binds office.

tsa-a20-v63.speaker: Teacher (injunction)
tsa-a20-v63.question: How strictly?
premises: iti tāṃ sarvathā caret — thus do it in every way.

tsa-a20-v64.speaker: Teacher (guru-rite)
tsa-a20-v64.question: What is the rite?
premises: tatra svāstikaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā ... pīṭhaṃ ... adhvānaṃ pūjayitvā tatpīṭhaṃ tena adhiṣṭhāpya — draw svāstika, give golden seat, worship the path-course, install the seat.
tasmai pūjāṃ kṛtvā tarpaṇaṃ bhojanaṃ dakṣiṇām ātmānam iti nivedya — to him worship, sating, meal, gift, self offered.
naivedyocchiṣṭaṃ prārthya vanditvā svayaṃ prāśya cakrapūjāṃ kuryāt — begging leavings, bowing, tasting, do wheel-worship.
tsa-a20-v64.inference: Seat, path, self-offering; leavings tasted; wheel-worship close.

tsa-a20-v65.speaker: Teacher (seal)
tsa-a20-v65.question: What was this?
premises: ita gurupūjāvidhiḥ — is guru-worship rule.
uncertainties: ita form obscure; seal-sense from position.

tsa-a20-v01.plain_english: There — the initiation for the perfection of refinement for those fit for knowledge, and the with-seed release-initiation for those incapable of it: once it is performed, the guru should teach the lifelong remaining course.
tsa-a20-v01.sanskrit_cite: tatra yā dīkṣā saṃskārasiddhyai jñānayogyān prati yā ca tadaśaktān prati mokṣadīkṣā sabījā tasyāṃ kṛtāyām ājīvaṃ śeṣavartanaṃ guruḥ upadiśet

tsa-a20-v02.plain_english: Here the remaining course is threefold — daily, occasional, and wished-for. The last belongs to the practitioner alone; it is not settled here.
tsa-a20-v02.sanskrit_cite: tatra nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyam iti trividhaṃ śeṣavartanam antyaṃ ca sādhakasyaiva tat na iha niścetavyam

tsa-a20-v03.plain_english: Here what occurs regularly is the daily; identity-with-that alone is the occasional; serving it are twilight worship, daily practice, festival day, sacred thread, and the rest.
tsa-a20-v03.sanskrit_cite: tatra niyatabhavaṃ nityaṃ tanmayībhāva eva naimittikaṃ tadupayogi saṃdhyopāsanaṃ pratyaham anuṣṭhānaṃ parvadinaṃ pavitrakam ityādi

tsa-a20-v04.plain_english: That too is daily, by the fixedness of its own time — say some.
tsa-a20-v04.sanskrit_cite: tad api nityaṃ svakālanaiyatyāt iti kecit

tsa-a20-v05.plain_english: But the occasional, even for those who abide in his teaching, is irregular — namely the coming of the guru and his circle, their festival day, the day of gaining knowledge, and the rest — say some.
tsa-a20-v05.sanskrit_cite: naimittikaṃ tu tacchāsanasthānām api aniyatam tadyathā gurutadvargāgamanaṃ tatparvadinaṃ jñānalābhadinam ityādikam iti kecit

tsa-a20-v06.plain_english: Here fixed worship, twilight worship, guru worship, festival worship, and sacred thread — unfailing, all.
tsa-a20-v06.sanskrit_cite: tatra niyatapūjā saṃdhyopāsā gurupūjā parvapūjā pavitrakam iti avaśyaṃbhāvi

tsa-a20-v07.plain_english: Occasional are the gaining of knowledge, the gaining of scripture, the coming to the house of the guru's circle, their days of birth-refinement and departure, worldly festival, exposition of scripture, beginning, middle, and end, the seeing of deities, gathering, dream command, and the gaining of release from the rule — this occasional is the cause of special worship.
tsa-a20-v07.sanskrit_cite: naimittikam jñānalābhaḥ śāstralābho gurutadvargagṛhāgamanaṃ tadīyajanmasaṃskāraprāyaṇadināni laukikotsavaḥ śāstravyākhyā ādimadhyāntā devatādarśanaṃ melakaṃ svapnājñā samayaniṣkṛtilābhaḥ ity etat naimittikaṃ viśeṣārcanakāraṇam

tsa-a20-v08.plain_english: Here, to the initiated disciple one should transmit by mouth-lineage alone the chief mantra — potent, its essence the flashing-forth of consciousness, unwritten. Then, to perfect identity-with-that, the disciple should practice identity at the twilights; through that door, at all times, to perfect the gaining of such refinement; and daily one should worship the Supreme Lord on the altar or on the liṅga.
tsa-a20-v08.sanskrit_cite: tatra kṛtadīkṣākasya śiṣyasya pradhānaṃ mantraṃ savīryakaṃ saṃvittisphuraṇasāram alikhitaṃ vaktrāgamenaiva arpayet tataḥ tanmayībhāvasiddhyarthaṃ sa śiṣyaḥ saṃdhyāsu tanmayībhāvābhyāsaṃ kuryāt taddvāreṇa sarvakālaṃ tathāvidhasaṃskāralābhasiddhyarthaṃ pratyahaṃ ca parameśvaraṃ ca sthaṇḍile vā liṅge vā abhyarcayet

tsa-a20-v09.plain_english: Here, on an altar delightful to the heart, meditated upon like a stainless mirror — having seen one's very form, non-different from the worshippable wheel of deities, as it were mirrored in a body — one should worship with heart-delighting flowers, scents, wine, libations, food-offerings, smoke, lamps, gifts, praise, song, music, dance, and the rest; murmur; chant praise — to obtain doubt-free identity-with-that.
tsa-a20-v09.sanskrit_cite: tatra hṛdye sthaṇḍile vimalamakuravad dhyāte svam eva rūpaṃ yājyadevatācakrābhinnaṃ mūrtibimbitam iva dṛṣṭvā hṛdyapuṣpagandhāsavatarpaṇanaivedyadhūpadīpopahārastutigītavādyanṛttādinā pūjayet japet stuvīta tanmayībhāvam aśaṅkitaṃ labdhum

tsa-a20-v10.plain_english: For in a mirror, for one gazing ceaselessly at one's own face, certainty of its nature comes swiftly. And here no sequence is chief — apart from identity-with-that.
tsa-a20-v10.sanskrit_cite: ādarśe hi svamukham aviratam avalokayataḥ tatsvarūpaniścitiḥ acireṇaiva bhavet na cātra kaścit kramaḥ pradhānam ṛte tanmayībhāvāt

tsa-a20-v11.plain_english: Entered into identity with the supreme mantra, his beast-latency stain wiped away, his whole snare-net of bonds melted by the penetration of devotion's taste — whatever heart dwells in that is highest to be taken up: so say our gurus.
tsa-a20-v11.sanskrit_cite: paramantratanmayībhāvāviṣṭasya nivṛttapaśuvāsanākalaṅkasya bhaktirasānuvedhavidrutasamastapāśajālasya yat adhivasati hṛdayaṃ tad eva paramam upādeyam iti asmadguravaḥ

tsa-a20-v12.plain_english: Having lain down upon it, the ultimate-minded flashes forth the flood of being as light — which —
tsa-a20-v12.sanskrit_cite: adhiśayya pāramārthikaḥ bhāvaprasaraṃ prakāśam ullasati yā

tsa-a20-v13.plain_english: Supreme-nectar-vision-ness: by her they are worshipped — the knowers of the secret.

tsa-a20-v14.plain_english: Having prepared the ground, sprinkled in the moment with the unction of wonder-taste — with taken flowers, mentally, own-being's blossoms exuding their own perfume.
tsa-a20-v14.sanskrit_cite: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ

tsa-a20-v15.plain_english: From the course of the priceless cup of my heart, brimmed with bliss's nectar — you, together with the Goddess, in the body, God's temple — I worship day and night.

tsa-a20-v16.plain_english: Contemplating within the sense stated in the two verses, one should contemplate the wheel of deities.
tsa-a20-v16.sanskrit_cite: iti ślokadvayoktam artham antar bhāvayan devatācakraṃ bhāvayet

tsa-a20-v17.plain_english: Then the showing of seals, murmuring, and the offering of that.

tsa-a20-v18.plain_english: Dismissal through oneness with the one to be awakened.

tsa-a20-v19.plain_english: The chief food-offering one should eat oneself, or cast it all into water — for the water-born living are previously initiated, through the oblation-food: so say the scripture-knowers.
tsa-a20-v19.sanskrit_cite: mukhyaṃ naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyāt sarvaṃ vā jale kṣipet jalajā hi prāṇinaḥ pūrvadīkṣitāḥ carubhojanadvāreṇa iti āgamavidaḥ

tsa-a20-v20.plain_english: But where cats, mice, dogs, and the rest are eaten, doubt is born — toward hell. Even the knower, from the wish to grace the world, should not do such a thing; or, leaving the world behind, one should abide. Thus is the altar-sacrifice.
tsa-a20-v20.sanskrit_cite: mārjāramūṣakaśvādibhakṣaṇe tu śaṅkā janitā nirayāya iti jñānī api lokānugrahecchayā na tādṛk kuryāt lokaṃ vā parityajya āsīta iti sthaṇḍilayāgaḥ

tsa-a20-v21.plain_english: Now on the liṅga: there one should not install the liṅga with secret mantras — especially not the manifest. On those installed before, one should perform worship in the order of invocation and dismissal, taking the installed as support.
tsa-a20-v21.sanskrit_cite: atha liṅge tatra na rahasyamantraiḥ liṅgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet viśeṣāt vyaktam iti pūrvapratiṣṭhiteṣu āvāhanavisarjanakrameṇa pūjāṃ kuryāt ādhāratayā

tsa-a20-v22.plain_english: There — guru's body, one's own body, the Śakti's body, the book of secret scripture, the hero's cup, the rosary, the weapon, the arrow-thing, the pearl, the golden, the thing made of flowers, scents, substances, and heart-pleasing objects, or the mirror — one should worship as the liṅga.
tsa-a20-v22.sanskrit_cite: tatra gurudehaṃ svadehaṃ śaktidehaṃ rahasyaśāstrapustakaṃ vīrapātram akṣasūtraṃ prāharaṇaṃ bāṇīyaṃ mauktikaṃ sauvarṇaṃ puṣpagandhadravyādihṛdyavastukṛtaṃ makuraṃ vā liṅgam arcayet

tsa-a20-v23.plain_english: There — by the power of the support alone comes ever-greater mantra-success: thus the earlier is ever chief, since mantras follow the support's qualities; and there, in each goal to be won, each is chief: so say the scripture-gurus.
tsa-a20-v23.sanskrit_cite: tatra ca ādhārabalād eva adhikādhikamantrasiddhiḥ bhavati iti pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ pradhānam ādhāraguṇānuvidhāyitvāt ca mantrāṇāṃ tatra tatra sādhye tattatpradhānam iti śāstraguravaḥ

tsa-a20-v24.plain_english: Everywhere, the pride of non-difference from the Supreme Lord alone is the highest refinement.

tsa-a20-v26.plain_english: Here general, general-general, general-special, special-general, special, and special-special: thus sixfold is festival, from the completion of the rite.
tsa-a20-v26.sanskrit_cite: tatra sāmānyaṃ sāmānyasāmānyaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣo viśeṣasāmānyaṃ viśeṣo viśeṣaviśeṣaś ca iti ṣoḍhā parva

tsa-a20-v27.plain_english: From the completion of the rite.

tsa-a20-v28.plain_english: Here in every month the first and fifth days are general; the fourth, eighth, ninth, fourteenth, and fifteenth of both fortnights are general-general; on both of these too, in the fitting planet-and-star conjunctions on each stated lunar day, general-special. The first night-quarter of Mārgaśīrṣa, on the dark ninth; midnight of Pauṣa, on the dark ninth; midnight of Māgha, on the bright fifteenth; midday of Phālguna, on the bright twelfth; of Caitra, on the bright thirteenth; of Vaiśākha, on the dark eighth; of Jyaiṣṭha, on the dark ninth; on the first day of Āṣāḍha; the fore-part of Śrāvaṇa's day, on the dark eleventh; midday of Bhādrapada, on the bright sixth; the bright-ninth day of Āśvayuja; the first night-quarter of Kārttika, on the bright ninth: thus the special festival.
tsa-a20-v28.sanskrit_cite: tatra māsi māsi prathamaṃ pañcamaṃ dinaṃ sāmānyam caturthāṣṭamanavamacaturdaśapañcadaśāni dvayor api pakṣayoḥ sāmānyasāmānyam anayor ubhayor api rāśyoḥ vakṣyamāṇatattattithyucitagrahanakṣatrayoge sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ mārgaśīrṣasya prathamarātribhāgaḥ kṛṣṇanavamyām pauṣasya tu rātrimadhyaṃ kṛṣṇanavamyām māghasya rātrimadhyaṃ śuklapañcadaśyām phālgunasya dinamadhyaṃ śukladvādaśyām caitrasya śuklatrayodaśyām vaiśākhasya kṛṣṇāṣṭamyām jyaiṣṭhasya kṛṣṇanavamyām āṣāḍhasya prathame dine śrāvaṇasya divasapūrvabhāgaḥ kṛṣṇaikādaśyām bhādrapadasya dinamadhyaṃ śuklaṣaṣṭyām āśvayujasya śuklanavamīdinam kārttikasya prathamo rātribhāgaḥ śuklanavamyām iti viśeṣaparva

tsa-a20-v29.plain_english: Citrā with the moon, Maghā with Jupiter, Tiṣya with the moon, Pūrva-phalgunī with Mercury, Śravaṇa with Mercury, Śatabhiṣak with the moon, Diti's two, Rohiṇī with Venus, Viśākhā with Jupiter, Śravaṇa with the moon: thus.
tsa-a20-v29.sanskrit_cite: citrācandrau maghājīvau tiṣyacandrau pūrvaphālgunībudhau śravaṇabudhau śatabhiṣakcandrau dityau rohiṇīśukrau viśākhābṛhaspatī śravaṇacandrau iti

tsa-a20-v30.plain_english: If in Mārgaśīrṣa-first order they come in due number, excluding Āśvayuja — then special-special.
tsa-a20-v30.sanskrit_cite: yadi mārgaśīrṣādikrameṇa yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bhavati āśvayujaṃ varjayitvā tadā viśeṣaviśeṣaḥ

tsa-a20-v31.plain_english: If another special falls on another festival, then that is an after-festival, they say.
tsa-a20-v31.sanskrit_cite: anyaviśeṣaś cet anyaparvaṇi tadā tat anuparva ity āhuḥ

tsa-a20-v32.plain_english: And in star-and-planet conjunction, the hour is not chief.

tsa-a20-v33.plain_english: The lunar day alone — from special gain; but continuity of after-rite time on festival day is chief. By the primacy of the after-rite: of festival rites, after-rite, image-rite, and wheel-rite are synonyms.
tsa-a20-v33.sanskrit_cite: tither eva viśeṣalābhāt anuyāgakālānuvṛttis tu parvadine mukhyā anuyāgaprādhānyāt parvayāgānām anuyāgo mūrtiyāgaḥ cakrayāgaḥ iti paryāyāḥ

tsa-a20-v34.plain_english: Here the guru, his circle with offspring, the knower of reality, the maiden, the outcast woman, the courtesan, the bleeding woman, or the truth-knowing woman: in the wheel-rite the chief to be worshipped — especially all together.
tsa-a20-v34.sanskrit_cite: tatra guruḥ tadvargyaḥ sasaṃtānaḥ tattvavit kanyā antyā veśyā aruṇā tattvavedinī vā iti cakrayāge mukhyapūjyāḥ viśeṣāt sāmastyena

tsa-a20-v35.plain_english: Here in the middle the guru, in his covering-order — from the guru down to the bound ones, hero and power in turn: thus seated in wheel or in row, then with scents, smoke, flowers, and the rest in order one should worship. Then, having contemplated the vessel as Sadāśiva-formed, having filled it with wine meditated as Śakti-nectar, having worshipped there the enjoyer-power as Śiva, having thereby sated the wheel of deities, having contemplated the meeting of the triad, man, power, and Śiva in nature, in the order of the descent of coverings — with primacy of release and enjoyment, without and within — one should perform sating; then in the order of re-circulation: thus the complete circling nourishes the wheel.
tsa-a20-v35.sanskrit_cite: tatra madhye guruḥ tadāvaraṇakrameṇa gurvādisamayyantaṃ vīraḥ śaktiḥ iti krameṇa ity evaṃ cakrasthityā vā paṅktisthityā vā āsīta tato gandhadhūpapuṣpādibhiḥ krameṇa pūjayet tataḥ pātraṃ sadāśivarūpaṃ dhyātvā śaktyamṛtadhyātena āsavena pūrayitvā tatra bhoktrīṃ śaktiṃ śivatayā pūjayitvā tayaiva devatācakratarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā naraśaktiśivātmakatritayamelakaṃ dhyātvā āvaraṇāvataraṇakrameṇa mokṣabhogaprādhānyaṃ bahir antaś ca tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ pratisaṃcaraṇakrameṇa evaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇaṃ cakraṃ puṣṇāti

tsa-a20-v36.plain_english: Here, having placed the universe-made vessel on the base, having sated the wheel of deities, one should sate oneself with the saluted vessel. If no vessel: auspicious folded shell-hands; or with the right hand shaped as a vessel — auspicious — with the two hands, the right laid above, made jointless, folded shell-hands; with the falling drops the vetālas and guhyakas are pleased, by the flow Bhairava. Here entry is to be given to no one; if by mistake one has entered, one should make no doubt; having made up one's mind, one should perform the wheel-rite twice over. Then fried foods, meals, and the rest should be scattered freely before them, as desired — in a hidden house or, without code-names, one should join all by the word 'deity': thus is the hero-mixture rite.
tsa-a20-v36.sanskrit_cite: tatra ādhāre viśvamayaṃ pātraṃ sthāpayitvā devatācakraṃ tarpayitvā svātmānaṃ vanditena tena tarpayet pātrābhāve bhadraṃ vellitaśuktiḥ vā dakṣahastena pātrākāraṃ bhadraṃ dvābhyām uparigatadakṣiṇābhyāṃ niḥsaṃdhīkṛtābhyām vellitaśuktiḥ patadbhiḥ bindubhiḥ vetālaguhyakāḥ saṃtuṣyanti dhārayā bhairavaḥ atra praveśo na kasyacit deyaḥ pramādāt praviṣṭasya vicāraṃ na kuryāt kṛtvā punar dviguṇaṃ cakrayāgaṃ kuryāt tato 'vadaṃśān bhojanādīn ca agre yatheṣṭaṃ vikīryeta guptagṛhe vā saṃketābhidhānavarjaṃ devatāśabdena sarvān yojayet iti vīrasaṃkarayāgaḥ

tsa-a20-v37.plain_english: Then at the end with gifts, betel, clothes, and the rest one should satisfy them: thus this is the most excellent image-rite.
tsa-a20-v37.sanskrit_cite: tato 'nte dakṣiṇātāmbūlavastrādibhiḥ tarpayet iti pradhānatamo 'yaṃ mūrtiyāgaḥ

tsa-a20-v38.plain_english: Even the unseen-maṇḍala one, by the image-rite worshipping the festival days, within a year alone gains the fruit stated for putrakas — without twilight practice and the rest. Thus for the old, the enjoyers, and women is this rule: when power has descended, to be taught by the guru.
tsa-a20-v38.sanskrit_cite: adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'pi mūrtiyāgena parvadināni pūjayan varṣād eva putrakoktaṃ phalam eti vinā saṃdhyānuṣṭhānādibhiḥ iti vṛddhānāṃ bhogināṃ strīṇāṃ vidhir ayam śaktipāte sati upadeṣṭavyo guruṇā

tsa-a20-v40.plain_english: And it, in the Ratnamālā, the Triśiromata, the Siddhāmata, and the rest, is preceded by rule and fulfills the Lord's command; and this is said in the Tantrāloka: without the sacred thread, all is fruitless.
tsa-a20-v40.sanskrit_cite: sa ca śrīratnamālātriśiromataśrīsiddhāmatādau vidhipūrvakaḥ pārameśvarājñāpūrakaś ca uktaṃ caitat śrītantrāloke vinā pavitrakeṇa sarvaṃ niṣphalam iti

tsa-a20-v41.plain_english: Here, from bright Āṣāḍha up to the Kula-full-moon day's end, the sacred thread is to be done; Kārttika's dark fifteenth fulfills the Kula-wheel and the daily wheel: so say the knowers of the Nitya-tantra.
tsa-a20-v41.sanskrit_cite: tatra āṣāḍhaśuklāt kulapūrṇimādināntaṃ kāryaṃ pavitrakam tatra kārttikakṛṣṇapañcadaśī kulacakraṃ nityācakraṃ pūrayati iti śrīnityātantravidaḥ

tsa-a20-v42.plain_english: Māgha's bright fifteenth: so say the knowers of Bhairavakulormi.

tsa-a20-v43.plain_english: The southern-course-end fifteenth: so say the knowers of the Tantrasadbhāva.

tsa-a20-v44.plain_english: Here, according to one's means, having worshipped the God, having sated with oblation, one should give the sacred thread: from gold-, pearl-, and jewel-made beginning, one should make it even down to cloth, thread, cotton, and kuśa-grass-wombed.
tsa-a20-v44.sanskrit_cite: tatra vibhavena devaṃ pūjayitvā āhutyā tarpayitvā pavitrakaṃ dadyāt sauvarṇamuktāratnaviracitāt prabhṛti paṭasūtrakārpāsakuśagarbhāntam api kuryāt

tsa-a20-v45.plain_english: And that with tattva-number knots, and with pada, kalā, world, letter, and mantra-number knots: one knee-ending, another navel-ending, another throat-ending, another on the head — thus four sacred threads to the God and to the guru, contemplating forms completely full of all paths, one should give; to the rest, one.
tsa-a20-v45.sanskrit_cite: tac ca tattvasaṃkhyagranthikaṃ padakalābhuvanavarṇamantrasaṃkhyagranthi ca jānvantam ekaṃ nābhyantam aparaṃ kaṇṭhāntam anyat śirasi anyat iti catvāri pavitrakāṇi devāya gurave ca samastādhvaparipūrṇatadrūpabhāvanena dadyāt śeṣebhya ekam iti

tsa-a20-v46.plain_english: Then a great festival is to be held — the four-month rite, seven days and three days: thus chief and fallback courses. When there are means, monthly the sacred thread, or in the four months, or once. In not doing it, one should murmur expiation. Even the knower, even possessed of means, incurs by not doing; in greed-covered non-doing of knowledge, from the disgrace of knowledge.
tsa-a20-v46.sanskrit_cite: tato mahotsavaḥ kāryaḥ cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ ca iti mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ sati vibhave māsi māsi pavitrakam atha vā caturṣu māseṣu atha vā sakṛt tadakaraṇe prāyaścittaṃ japet jñānī api sambhavadvitto 'pi akaraṇe pratyavaiti lobhopahitajñānākaraṇe jñānanindāpatteḥ

tsa-a20-v47.plain_english: When, even having attained wisdom, the Lord's teaching is defiled — then one needs expiation.
tsa-a20-v47.sanskrit_cite: yadā prāpyāpi vijñānaṃ dūṣitaṃ parameśaśāsanaṃ tadā prāyaścittī

tsa-a20-v49.plain_english: Thus: this is the sacred-thread rule.

tsa-a20-v50.plain_english: At knowledge-gaining and the rest, at the end of worldly festival too — everywhere, excess of consciousness-blaze and the nearness of the deity-wheel especially come about: thus, considering such excess, just such a distinction, in after-rite and the rest, one should perform.
tsa-a20-v50.sanskrit_cite: jñānalābhādau laukikotsavānte 'pi sarvatra saṃvidullāsādhikyaṃ devatācakrasaṃnidhiḥ viśeṣato bhavati iti tathāvidhādhikyaparyālocanayā tathāvidham eva viśeṣam anuyāgādau kuryāt

tsa-a20-v52.plain_english: One should request the guru, complete in all scriptures, for the sake of exposition — he too, for his own disciple or even another's, should expound the scripture fit for fit refinement; even for one abiding in a lower teaching, from compassion, his heart made hopeful by the prospect of a descent of power manifested by the Lord's varied will, one should expound — excluding secret instruction.
tsa-a20-v52.sanskrit_cite: sarvaśāstrasampūrṇaṃ guruṃ vyākhyārtham abhyarthayeta so 'pi svaśiṣyāya paraśiṣyāyāpi vā samucitasaṃskārocitaṃ śāstraṃ vyācakṣīta adharaśāsanasthāyāpi karuṇāvaśāt īśvarecchāvaicitryodbhāvitaśaktipātasambhāvanābhāvitahṛdayo vyācakṣīta marmopadeśavarjam

tsa-a20-v53.plain_english: There, exposition performed for the devoted, seated low, with speech, mind, and body restrained, becomes fruitful. First, on the ground smeared with perfumes and the rest, having drawn or resolved: a lotus-base, four-cornered, a lotus-triad, in the middle of the lotus Vāgīśī, on left and right Gaṇapati and the guru — one should worship; on the base-lotus, the wish-granting deity of exposition.
tsa-a20-v53.sanskrit_cite: tatra nimnāsanasthitebhyaḥ tatparebhyo niyamitavāṅmanaḥkāyebhyo vyākhyā kriyamāṇā phalavatī bhavati prathamaṃ gandhādiliptāyāṃ bhuvi ullikhya saṃkalpya vā padmādhāraṃ caturaśraṃ padmatrayaṃ padmamadhye vāgīśīṃ vāmadakṣiṇayoḥ gaṇapatigurū ca pūjayet ādhārapadme vyākhyeyakalpadevatām

tsa-a20-v54.plain_english: Then, having sated the wheel with the common offering-vessel rite, one should expound: the text of aphorism, sentence, and chapter, uncontradicted before and after — first joining the position rightly, and rightly refuting; proving the provandum, revealing the drift — one should expound to the chapter's end, no more; even there, at each section's end, sating and worship — until the exposition is complete.
tsa-a20-v54.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ sāmānyārghapātrayogena cakraṃ tarpayet tato vyācakṣīta sūtravākyapaṭalagrantham pūrvāparāviruddhaṃ kurvan tantrāvṛttiprasaṅgasamuccayavikalpādiśāstranyāyaucityena pūrvaṃ pakṣaṃ samyak ghaṭayitvā samyak ca dūṣayan sādhyaṃ sādhayan tātparyavṛttiṃ pradarśayan paṭalāntaṃ vyācakṣīta nādhikam tatrāpi vastvante vastvante tarpaṇaṃ pūjanam iti yāvad vyākhyāsamāptiḥ

tsa-a20-v55.plain_english: Then too, having worshipped, having dismissed the knowledge-seat, having smeared, one should cast it into the deep.
tsa-a20-v55.sanskrit_cite: tato 'pi pūjayitvā vidyāpīṭhaṃ visarjya upalipya agādhe tat kṣepayet

tsa-a20-v58.plain_english: Though for one established in the knowledge of reality there is no expiation and the rest at all, yet to grace those who partake of release through conduct alone, one should display the course of conduct.
tsa-a20-v58.sanskrit_cite: yady api tattvajñānaniṣṭhasya prāyaścittādi na kiṃcit tathāpi caryāmātrād eva mokṣabhāginaḥ tān anugrahītum ācāravartanīṃ darśayet

tsa-a20-v59.plain_english: But the truth-unknowing one, whose enjoyment and release hang on conduct alone — if the rule is transgressed and, not performing expiation, he remains — for a hundred years he becomes an eater of raw flesh: thus the expiation rule is to be stated. There, in woman-slaying there is no expiation; elsewhere, having known strength and weakness, one should repeat the unbroken Goddess Mālinī from one time onward up to three hundred thousand, until doubt falls away. At its end, special worship; even there, the wheel-rite — for it everywhere remains.
tsa-a20-v59.sanskrit_cite: atattvajñānī tu caryaikāyattabhogamokṣaḥ samayollaṅghane kṛte prāyaścittam akurvan varṣaśataṃ kravyādo bhavatīti iti prāyaścittavidhiḥ vaktavyaḥ tatra strīvadhe prāyaścittaṃ nāsti anyatra tu balābalaṃ jñātvā akhaṇḍāṃ bhagavatīṃ mālinīm ekavārāt prabhṛti trilakṣāntam āvartayet yāvat śaṅkāvicyutiḥ bhavati tadante viśeṣapūjā tatrāpi cakrayāgaḥ sa hi sarvatra śeṣabhūtaḥ

tsa-a20-v62.plain_english: At the close of all rites, when the rite has been gathered in, on the next day one should perform guru-worship — for before, as a limb of the rite he is gratified, but not chiefly: thus, not performing it chiefly, bound by the bond of office, one remains bound.
tsa-a20-v62.sanskrit_cite: sarvayāgānteṣu upasaṃhṛte yāge aparedyuḥ gurupūjāṃ kuryāt pūrvaṃ hi sa vidhyaṅgatayā toṣito na tu prādhānyena iti tāṃ prādhānyena akurvan adhikārabandhena baddho bhavati

tsa-a20-v63.plain_english: Thus one should perform it in every way.

tsa-a20-v64.plain_english: There, having drawn a svāstika maṇḍala, there having given a golden seat, there having worshipped the entire path-course, having established that seat thereby, having performed worship to him, sating, meal, gift, and self — thus having offered, having begged the food-leavings, having bowed, having tasted oneself, one should perform wheel-worship.
tsa-a20-v64.sanskrit_cite: tatra svāstikaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tatra sauvarṇaṃ pīṭhaṃ dattvā tatra samastam adhvānaṃ pūjayitvā tatpīṭhaṃ tena adhiṣṭhāpya tasmai pūjāṃ kṛtvā tarpaṇaṃ bhojanaṃ dakṣiṇām ātmānam iti nivedya naivedyocchiṣṭaṃ prārthya vanditvā svayaṃ prāśya cakrapūjāṃ kuryāt

essence: Two initiations — refinement-perfection for the knowledge-fit, with-seed release for the incapable — then the guru teaches the lifelong remainder.
Remainder threefold: daily, occasional, wished-for; the last practitioner-only, undecided here.
Daily is the recurrent; occasional is identity-with-that; its servants: twilight worship, practice, festival, thread.
Fixed-time occasional counts as daily — some say.
Occasional irregular even for insiders: guru's coming, festivals, knowledge-days — some say.
Unfailing five: fixed, twilight, guru, festival worship, sacred thread.
Twelve occasions from knowledge-gain to rule-release cause special worship.
Unwritten potent mantra by mouth-lineage alone; twilight identity-practice; daily Lord-worship on altar or liṅga.
Mirror-meditated heart-altar; own form as deity-wheel body-mirrored; full offering train; doubt-free identity.
Ceaseless mirror-gazing swiftly certifies; no order chief but identity.
Stain gone, bonds melted: the indwelling heart highest to take up — our gurus.
Ultimate-minded flashes being-flood as light — open verse.
Supreme-nectar-vision: secret-knowers worshipped by her.
Wonder-sprinkled ground; mental own-being flowers exuding fragrance.
Priceless heart-cup; you with Goddess in body-temple worshipped day and night.
Two-verse sense internalized as wheel-contemplation.
Seal-showing, murmuring, offering of that.
Dismissal through unity with the to-be-awakened.
Eat the chief offering or water-cast it; water-born already initiated — scripture-knowers.
Impure eating barred even for knowers; withdrawal alternative; altar-rite sealed.
No secret-mantra liṅga installation; manifest preferred; installed ones worshipped in order as support.
Fourteen substitutes from guru's body to mirror worshippable as liṅga.
Support-power scales mantra-success; earlier supports chief; each goal its chief — scripture-gurus.
Non-difference-pride alone highest refinement, everywhere.
Festival rule opened.
Six festival grades from rite-completion.
Festival defined: rite-completion celebrated.
Monthly, fortnightly, conjunctional, twelve monthly specials: the full calendar.
Ten star-planet conjunction pairs.
Mārgaśīrṣa-first due order minus Āśvayuja: special-special.
Another special on another festival: after-festival, they say.
Conjunctions: hour not chief.
Tithi-gain; continuity chief; after-rite, image-rite, wheel-rite synonyms.
Nine-member wheel company; collective chief worship.
Center guru, covering-order, wheel or row; Sadāśiva-vessel with Śakti-nectar wine; enjoyer-as-Śiva; triad; descent; inside-outside; re-circulation completes the wheel.
Universe-vessel; self sated with it; hand-vessel substitute; drops please vetālas, flow Bhairava; no entry; doubtless double-rite remedy; hidden-house deity-name union: hero-mixture rite.
Gift-sating close; most excellent image-rite.
Unseen-maṇḍala image-rite on festivals gains putraka-fruit within a year; for old, enjoyers, women with śaktipāta, guru-taught.
Sacred-thread rule opened.
Ratnamālā and the rest precede; Lord's command fulfilled; Tantrāloka seal: no thread, no fruit.
Āṣāḍha-to-Māgha season; Kārttika dark fifteenth double fulfillment — Nitya-tantra view.
Māgha bright fifteenth — Bhairavakulormi view.
Southern-course-end fifteenth — Tantrasadbhāva view.
Means-graded materials gold to kuśa-grass.
Four body-length threads with adhva-knot counts for God and guru; one for the rest.
Great festival and fallback courses; lapse atoned by murmuring; means-withholding disgraces knowledge.
Attained wisdom defiling the teaching: expiation case.
Statement-seal on the case.
Sacred-thread rule closed.
Festival excess-blaze calls for matching after-rite distinction.
Exposition rule opened.
Request the complete guru; expound fit text to fit disciples, even lower ones from compassion on śaktipāta-hope; secrets excluded.
Low devoted restrained seats; perfumed ground; lotus-maṇḍala with Vāgīśī center.
Common-vessel sating; sūtra-text uncontradicted; join-then-refute; section-end sating; chapter-bound.
Worshipped, dismissed, smeared knowledge-seat cast in the deep.
Exposition rule closed.
Rule-expiation opened.
Established need none; conduct-sharers get the course shown.
Woman-slaying inexpiable; Mālinī repeated to three hundred thousand till doubt falls; wheel-rite everywhere remaining.
Rule-expiation closed.
Guru-worship rule opened.
Next-day chief guru-worship; limb-only before; omission binds office.
Unqualified injunction: do it every way.
Svāstika seat; path worshipped; self offered; leavings tasted; wheel-worship close.
Guru-worship rule sealed; ahnika ends.

rasa.justification: The ahnika legislates — days, knots, courses — and each rule lands as rest: calendar exactness settling into observance; wonder breaks through only in the wheel-rite (u35-36) and the mirror-gazing (u9-10).

sections.FUNCTION: Establishes the lifelong course after initiation (śeṣavartana): daily/occasional counts with minority views, the unfailing five, twelve occasions, mouth-lineage mantra transmission, mirror-contemplation identity, food and liṅga rules, support-power scaling, abheda-pride as supreme refinement — then the parvan calendar (six grades, conjunctions, rival school dates), the cakra/mūrti-yāga complex with hand-vessel and no-entry rules, the pavitraka system (season, materials, knot-counts, lapse), vyākhyā method (join-then-refute, chapter-bound), samaya-niṣkṛti (inexpiable breach, Mālinī count), and next-day chief guru-worship — closing the ahnika.
sections.KEY TERMS: śeṣavartana (lifelong remainder: nitya/naimittika/kāmya); tanmayībhāva (identity-with-that); vaktrāgama (mouth-lineage, unwritten); ādarśa-nyāya (mirror-certainty); parvan (festival: six grades; pūraṇād vidheḥ); anuparva (after-festival); nakṣatra-graha-yoga (ten conjunctions); cakrayāga/mūrtiyāga/anuyāga (synonyms by after-rite primacy); vellitaśukti (folded shell-hands vessel-substitute); vīrasaṃkara (hero-mixture rite); pavitraka (sacred thread: season, knots, lapse); vyākhyā (join-then-refute exposition); samayaniṣkṛti (rule-expiation; Mālinī count); gurupūjā (next-day chief worship).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Āhnika 20 carries the nitya/naimittika worship code between the dīkṣā ahnikas (a14–a16) and the Kaula close (a22); parvan/pavitraka detail parallels Tantrāloka 28; the cakra-yāga anticipates Tantrāloka 29's kula-yāga. Witnesses: Pradīpaka word-by-word (sanskrit-trikashaivism), Chakravarty translation (Ishwar Ashram), vishvasa English rendering — parallels, not sources.
sections.EXPLANATION: The ahnika runs: (1) charter — two initiations, lifelong course, threefold remainder with wished-for deferred, daily/occasional counts with ke-cit views, unfailing five, twelve occasions; (2) transmission and identity — unwritten mantra by mouth, twilight practice, daily worship, mirror-altar contemplation with full offerings, swiftness without order, guru heart-doctrine, two open verses, stotra pair on ground-rite and heart-cup worship, wheel-contemplation seal, seals-murmur-offer, unity-dismissal; (3) food, liṅga, support — eat-or-cast rule, impure-eating bar with withdrawal option, no secret-mantra installation, fourteen substitutes, support-power scaling, abheda-pride peak; (4) parvan — rule, six grades, rite-completion definition, full calendar, ten conjunctions, special-special computation, anuparvan, hour-subordination, synonym triad, nine-member company; (5) wheel rite — order, vessel-filling, enjoyer-as-Śiva, triad, descent, re-circulation, universe-vessel, hand substitute, drop/flow pleasures, no-entry with double-rite remedy, hidden-house deity-name union, gift close, putraka concession for old/enjoyers/women; (6) pavitraka — rule, triple warrant, season with rival school dates, means-graded materials, knot-counts and body-lengths, festival courses, lapse and disgrace, defilement case with statement-seal; (7) excess, exposition — blaze-excess distinction, exposition rule, fit-to-fit teaching with compassion, low-seat lotus-maṇḍala, join-then-refute method, section sating, deep dismissal; (8) niṣkṛti and guru — established need none, breach punishments, inexpiable breach, Mālinī count to doubt's fall, wheel remaining, next-day chief guru-worship with office-bond, unqualified injunction, seat-path-self rite with leavings, seal.
sections.BOUNDARY: Two genuine L0 forks adjudicated (vellitaśukti hand-pose; Mālinī-mantra). Anomalous print forms kept with flags: bāṇīyaṃ (u22), makuraṃ (u22), dityau (u29), kṛtvādhāradharāṃ junction (u14), mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ (u46), sambhavadvitto (u46), ita (u65), prāyaścittādi ending (u58), anvāpatkalpa series. Wished-for (kāmya) rite deferred in the doctrine — not reconstructed. Rival school dates recorded, not harmonized. OccultGuide/Chakravarty/Pradīpaka kept as witness-parallels only.
