lines: There — for the knowledge-fit, initiation to perfect refinement;
for the unfit, seeded release. Once given, the master teaches life's remainder.
tsa-a20-v01.sanskrit_cite: tatra yā dīkṣā saṃskārasiddhyai jñānayogyān prati yā ca tadaśaktān prati mokṣadīkṣā sabījā tasyāṃ kṛtāyām ājīvaṃ śeṣavartanaṃ guruḥ upadiśet

lines: Daily, occasional, longed-for: threefold remains the course.
The last is the practitioner's alone — here left undecided.
tsa-a20-v02.sanskrit_cite: tatra nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyam iti trividhaṃ śeṣavartanam antyaṃ ca sādhakasyaiva tat na iha niścetavyam

lines: What returns on time is daily; to be That, the occasional;
its servants — dusk-worship, practice, feast-day, sacred thread.
tsa-a20-v03.sanskrit_cite: tatra niyatabhavaṃ nityaṃ tanmayībhāva eva naimittikaṃ tadupayogi saṃdhyopāsanaṃ pratyaham anuṣṭhānaṃ parvadinaṃ pavitrakam ityādi

lines: Even that is daily, bound to its hour — so some.
tsa-a20-v04.sanskrit_cite: tad api nityaṃ svakālanaiyatyāt iti kecit

lines: But the occasional, though he dwell in the teaching, falls out of time —
master's coming, his feast, wisdom's day — so some.
tsa-a20-v05.sanskrit_cite: naimittikaṃ tu tacchāsanasthānām api aniyatam tadyathā gurutadvargāgamanaṃ tatparvadinaṃ jñānalābhadinam ityādikam iti kecit

lines: Set worship, dusk-worship, master-worship, feast-worship, the thread —
unfailing, all.
tsa-a20-v06.sanskrit_cite: tatra niyatapūjā saṃdhyopāsā gurupūjā parvapūjā pavitrakam iti avaśyaṃbhāvi

lines: Wisdom gained, scripture gained, the master's house approached,
birth-days, world-feasts, doctrine told, first midst and last, gods seen, conclave, dream-bid, dues cleared — this occasional calls for heightened praise.
tsa-a20-v07.sanskrit_cite: naimittikam jñānalābhaḥ śāstralābho gurutadvargagṛhāgamanaṃ tadīyajanmasaṃskāraprāyaṇadināni laukikotsavaḥ śāstravyākhyā ādimadhyāntā devatādarśanaṃ melakaṃ svapnājñā samayaniṣkṛtilābhaḥ ity etat naimittikaṃ viśeṣārcanakāraṇam

lines: To the sworn disciple give, by mouth alone, the chief spell —
potent, unwritten, flashing awareness' core. Then at each dusk rehearse identity with That;
through that door, at every hour, ripen such becoming; and daily adore the Highest — altar or emblem.
tsa-a20-v08.sanskrit_cite: tatra kṛtadīkṣākasya śiṣyasya pradhānaṃ mantraṃ savīryakaṃ saṃvittisphuraṇasāram alikhitaṃ vaktrāgamenaiva arpayet tataḥ tanmayībhāvasiddhyarthaṃ sa śiṣyaḥ saṃdhyāsu tanmayībhāvābhyāsaṃ kuryāt taddvāreṇa sarvakālaṃ tathāvidhasaṃskāralābhasiddhyarthaṃ pratyahaṃ ca parameśvaraṃ ca sthaṇḍile vā liṅge vā abhyarcayet

lines: On the heart's glad altar, glassed like a stainless mirror —
seeing your own shape, no other than the worshipped ring, body-mirrored —
with gladdening blooms and scents, wine, drink-gifts, dishes, smoke, lamps, presents, hymns, songs, strings, drums — adore, murmur, sing — to win undoubting That-ness.
tsa-a20-v09.sanskrit_cite: tatra hṛdye sthaṇḍile vimalamakuravad dhyāte svam eva rūpaṃ yājyadevatācakrābhinnaṃ mūrtibimbitam iva dṛṣṭvā hṛdyapuṣpagandhāsavatarpaṇanaivedyadhūpadīpopahārastutigītavādyanṛttādinā pūjayet japet stuvīta tanmayībhāvam aśaṅkitaṃ labdhum

lines: Who gazes unblinking at his face in glass
knows himself, and soon. No stepwise ladder leads — only That-ness.
tsa-a20-v10.sanskrit_cite: ādarśe hi svamukham aviratam avalokayataḥ tatsvarūpaniścitiḥ acireṇaiva bhavet na cātra kaścit kramaḥ pradhānam ṛte tanmayībhāvāt

lines: Steeped in supreme-spell That-ness, beast-stain gone,
the whole net of bondage melted by devotion's taste — whatever heart abides therein is highest prize: so speak our masters.
tsa-a20-v11.sanskrit_cite: paramantratanmayībhāvāviṣṭasya nivṛttapaśuvāsanākalaṅkasya bhaktirasānuvedhavidrutasamastapāśajālasya yat adhivasati hṛdayaṃ tad eva paramam upādeyam iti asmadguravaḥ

lines: Couched upon it, the true-aimed mind
flares the flood of being into light — which —
tsa-a20-v12.sanskrit_cite: adhiśayya pāramārthikaḥ bhāvaprasaraṃ prakāśam ullasati yā

lines: Supreme-deathless sight: by her they are adored —
the knowers of the secret.
Ground prepared, dew-fresh with wonder's taste —
with plucked mind-flowers, own-natured, breathing their own sweet.
tsa-a20-v14.sanskrit_cite: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ

lines: From my heart's cup, brimmed with bliss-deathless, priceless —
you, Goddess beside you, in the body's god-house — I praise by day and night.
The two-verse sense revolved within — contemplate the god-ring.
tsa-a20-v16.sanskrit_cite: iti ślokadvayoktam artham antar bhāvayan devatācakraṃ bhāvayet

lines: Then seal displayed, murmur, and the gift thereof.
Dismissal — one with what must wake.
Eat the first portion, or drown it all —
for water's children were christened before, through the cake they share: so the lore-men say.
tsa-a20-v19.sanskrit_cite: mukhyaṃ naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyāt sarvaṃ vā jale kṣipet jalajā hi prāṇinaḥ pūrvadīkṣitāḥ carubhojanadvāreṇa iti āgamavidaḥ

lines: But to dine on cat and mouse and dog breeds doubt — hellward.
Not even the wise, to bless the world, should stoop; or quit the world and sit. So ends the altar-rite.
tsa-a20-v20.sanskrit_cite: mārjāramūṣakaśvādibhakṣaṇe tu śaṅkā janitā nirayāya iti jñānī api lokānugrahecchayā na tādṛk kuryāt lokaṃ vā parityajya āsīta iti sthaṇḍilayāgaḥ

lines: Now for the emblem: raise no sign with hidden spells —
least of all the manifest. Where signs stand raised of old, in coming-and-going order, worship — the old ones bearing all.
tsa-a20-v21.sanskrit_cite: atha liṅge tatra na rahasyamantraiḥ liṅgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet viśeṣāt vyaktam iti pūrvapratiṣṭhiteṣu āvāhanavisarjanakrameṇa pūjāṃ kuryāt ādhāratayā

lines: Master's frame, your frame, Her frame, the secret book,
hero's bowl, bead-string, spear, arrow-gear, pearl, gold —
wrought of blooms and scents and dear stuff, or the glass — worship as the sign.
tsa-a20-v22.sanskrit_cite: tatra gurudehaṃ svadehaṃ śaktidehaṃ rahasyaśāstrapustakaṃ vīrapātram akṣasūtraṃ prāharaṇaṃ bāṇīyaṃ mauktikaṃ sauvarṇaṃ puṣpagandhadravyādihṛdyavastukṛtaṃ makuraṃ vā liṅgam arcayet

lines: By the ground's might alone mantra-speed grows and grows —
the elder ground is ever chief, for spells track the ground they stand on;
and each goal crowns its own chief: so the scripture-masters.
tsa-a20-v23.sanskrit_cite: tatra ca ādhārabalād eva adhikādhikamantrasiddhiḥ bhavati iti pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ pradhānam ādhāraguṇānuvidhāyitvāt ca mantrāṇāṃ tatra tatra sādhye tattatpradhānam iti śāstraguravaḥ

lines: Everywhere, pride — no gap 'twixt me and the Highest —
alone the crowning culture.
Now the feast-law.
Common, common-common, common-rare, rare-common, rare, rare-rare —
sixfold the feast, born of the rite's fulfillment.
tsa-a20-v26.sanskrit_cite: tatra sāmānyaṃ sāmānyasāmānyaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣo viśeṣasāmānyaṃ viśeṣo viśeṣaviśeṣaś ca iti ṣoḍhā parva

lines: Born of the rite's fulfillment.
Month by month, first and fifth are common;
fourth, eighth, ninth, fourteenth, fifteenth of either half — common-common;
on both, when the due stars wed the due days — common-rare.
Mārgaśīrṣa's first night-watch, dark ninth; Pauṣa's midnight, dark ninth;
Māgha's midnight, bright fifteenth; Phālguna's noon, bright twelfth;
Caitra's bright thirteenth; Vaiśākha's dark eighth; Jyaiṣṭha's dark ninth;
Āṣāḍha's first day; Śrāvaṇa's fore-noon, dark eleventh;
Bhādrapada's noon, bright sixth; Āśvayuja's bright-ninth day;
Kārttika's first night-watch, bright ninth: so the rare feast.
tsa-a20-v28.sanskrit_cite: tatra māsi māsi prathamaṃ pañcamaṃ dinaṃ sāmānyam caturthāṣṭamanavamacaturdaśapañcadaśāni dvayor api pakṣayoḥ sāmānyasāmānyam anayor ubhayor api rāśyoḥ vakṣyamāṇatattattithyucitagrahanakṣatrayoge sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ mārgaśīrṣasya prathamarātribhāgaḥ kṛṣṇanavamyām pauṣasya tu rātrimadhyaṃ kṛṣṇanavamyām māghasya rātrimadhyaṃ śuklapañcadaśyām phālgunasya dinamadhyaṃ śukladvādaśyām caitrasya śuklatrayodaśyām vaiśākhasya kṛṣṇāṣṭamyām jyaiṣṭhasya kṛṣṇanavamyām āṣāḍhasya prathame dine śrāvaṇasya divasapūrvabhāgaḥ kṛṣṇaikādaśyām bhādrapadasya dinamadhyaṃ śuklaṣaṣṭyām āśvayujasya śuklanavamīdinam kārttikasya prathamo rātribhāgaḥ śuklanavamyām iti viśeṣaparva

lines: Moon with Citrā, Jove with Maghā, Moon with Tiṣya, Witan with Fore-Phalgunī,
Witan with Ear, Moon with Hundred-Healers, Diti's twain,
Love with Rohiṇī, Preceptor with Branch, Moon with Ear again: so.
tsa-a20-v29.sanskrit_cite: citrācandrau maghājīvau tiṣyacandrau pūrvaphālgunībudhau śravaṇabudhau śatabhiṣakcandrau dityau rohiṇīśukrau viśākhābṛhaspatī śravaṇacandrau iti

lines: Count from Mārgaśīrṣa in due rank, dropping Āśvayuja —
then rarest-rare.
tsa-a20-v30.sanskrit_cite: yadi mārgaśīrṣādikrameṇa yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bhavati āśvayujaṃ varjayitvā tadā viśeṣaviśeṣaḥ

lines: If elsewhere a rarity lights another feast —
then after-feast, say they.
tsa-a20-v31.sanskrit_cite: anyaviśeṣaś cet anyaparvaṇi tadā tat anuparva ity āhuḥ

lines: When star meets planet, the hour bows out.
The day-starved moon-day alone — by special gain; but hold the after-rite's unbroken time on feast-day chief.
By after-rite's first rank: after-rite, image-rite, wheel-rite — one name in three.
tsa-a20-v33.sanskrit_cite: tither eva viśeṣalābhāt anuyāgakālānuvṛttis tu parvadine mukhyā anuyāgaprādhānyāt parvayāgānām anuyāgo mūrtiyāgaḥ cakrayāgaḥ iti paryāyāḥ

lines: Master, his line and sons, truth-knower, maid,
outcaste, wanton, monthly-bleeder, truth-knowing dame —
in the wheel, first-honored, all as one.
tsa-a20-v34.sanskrit_cite: tatra guruḥ tadvargyaḥ sasaṃtānaḥ tattvavit kanyā antyā veśyā aruṇā tattvavedinī vā iti cakrayāge mukhyapūjyāḥ viśeṣāt sāmastyena

lines: Midmost the master, ringed in veiling order — from master down to the last bound, hero, goddess by turns —
sit ringed or ranked. Then scent and smoke and blooms in turn adore.
The bowl beheld as Ever-bliss, brimmed with Her nectar-wine;
the tasting goddess praised as Śiva; by her the god-ring sated;
the triad — man, might, Śiva — one-natured, held in mind;
then in veil-descending order, release and relish first, within, without — sate;
then circling back again: so the whole round feeds the wheel.
tsa-a20-v35.sanskrit_cite: tatra madhye guruḥ tadāvaraṇakrameṇa gurvādisamayyantaṃ vīraḥ śaktiḥ iti krameṇa ity evaṃ cakrasthityā vā paṅktisthityā vā āsīta tato gandhadhūpapuṣpādibhiḥ krameṇa pūjayet tataḥ pātraṃ sadāśivarūpaṃ dhyātvā śaktyamṛtadhyātena āsavena pūrayitvā tatra bhoktrīṃ śaktiṃ śivatayā pūjayitvā tayaiva devatācakratarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā naraśaktiśivātmakatritayamelakaṃ dhyātvā āvaraṇāvataraṇakrameṇa mokṣabhogaprādhānyaṃ bahir antaś ca tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ pratisaṃcaraṇakrameṇa evaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇaṃ cakraṃ puṣṇāti

lines: On the ground set the world-bowl; sate the god-ring; sate yourself with the hailed.
No bowl? Folded shell-hands, blest; or the right hand bowled — blest —
two together, right above, seamless — folded shell-hands; falling drops delight the haunters, the stream delights the Dread.
None may enter here; the strayed-in doubt not; instead redouble the wheel-rite.
Fritters and dishes scatter freely before them, as they please —
in the hidden house, nameless, all gathered under 'god': so the heroes' mingling-rite.
tsa-a20-v36.sanskrit_cite: tatra ādhāre viśvamayaṃ pātraṃ sthāpayitvā devatācakraṃ tarpayitvā svātmānaṃ vanditena tena tarpayet pātrābhāve bhadraṃ vellitaśuktiḥ vā dakṣahastena pātrākāraṃ bhadraṃ dvābhyām uparigatadakṣiṇābhyāṃ niḥsaṃdhīkṛtābhyām vellitaśuktiḥ patadbhiḥ bindubhiḥ vetālaguhyakāḥ saṃtuṣyanti dhārayā bhairavaḥ atra praveśo na kasyacit deyaḥ pramādāt praviṣṭasya vicāraṃ na kuryāt kṛtvā punar dviguṇaṃ cakrayāgaṃ kuryāt tato 'vadaṃśān bhojanādīn ca agre yatheṣṭaṃ vikīryeta guptagṛhe vā saṃketābhidhānavarjaṃ devatāśabdena sarvān yojayet iti vīrasaṃkarayāgaḥ

lines: At the close with gifts and leaf and cloth sate them:
so this image-rite, first among rites.
tsa-a20-v37.sanskrit_cite: tato 'nte dakṣiṇātāmbūlavastrādibhiḥ tarpayet iti pradhānatamo 'yaṃ mūrtiyāgaḥ

lines: Though no circle ever seen, the feast-days kept by image-rite
within a year bear sons'-rite fruit, no dusk-rites needed.
So for the aged, the lovers, wives — when power falls, the master teaches.
tsa-a20-v38.sanskrit_cite: adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'pi mūrtiyāgena parvadināni pūjayan varṣād eva putrakoktaṃ phalam eti vinā saṃdhyānuṣṭhānādibhiḥ iti vṛddhānāṃ bhogināṃ strīṇāṃ vidhir ayam śaktipāte sati upadeṣṭavyo guruṇā

lines: Now the thread-law.
Through Jewel-Garland, Three-Peak, Perfect Lore the thread comes law-first, crowned with the Highest's bid —
and the Light-Hall declares: threadless, all is fruitless.
tsa-a20-v40.sanskrit_cite: sa ca śrīratnamālātriśiromataśrīsiddhāmatādau vidhipūrvakaḥ pārameśvarājñāpūrakaś ca uktaṃ caitat śrītantrāloke vinā pavitrakeṇa sarvaṃ niṣphalam iti

lines: From bright Āṣāḍha to Kula-full-moon's close wear the thread;
Kārttika's dark fifteenth fills either wheel: so Night-Tantra's knowers.
tsa-a20-v41.sanskrit_cite: tatra āṣāḍhaśuklāt kulapūrṇimādināntaṃ kāryaṃ pavitrakam tatra kārttikakṛṣṇapañcadaśī kulacakraṃ nityācakraṃ pūrayati iti śrīnityātantravidaḥ

lines: Māgha's bright fifteenth: so Bhairava's Wave-knowers.
The southward sun's last fifteenth: so Sadbhāva's knowers.
Worship the god as you can afford, libate and sate, then give the thread —
wrought from gold-and-gem down to mere cloth-thread, cotton, kuśa-bellied.
tsa-a20-v44.sanskrit_cite: tatra vibhavena devaṃ pūjayitvā āhutyā tarpayitvā pavitrakaṃ dadyāt sauvarṇamuktāratnaviracitāt prabhṛti paṭasūtrakārpāsakuśagarbhāntam api kuryāt

lines: Knotted with the count of principles, knotted with path-and-pitch-and-world-and-syllable-and-spell —
one to the knee, one to the navel, one to the throat, one crowned —
four threads to god and guide, brooding forms brimmed with every path; to the rest, one.
tsa-a20-v45.sanskrit_cite: tac ca tattvasaṃkhyagranthikaṃ padakalābhuvanavarṇamantrasaṃkhyagranthi ca jānvantam ekaṃ nābhyantam aparaṃ kaṇṭhāntam anyat śirasi anyat iti catvāri pavitrakāṇi devāya gurave ca samastādhvaparipūrṇatadrūpabhāvanena dadyāt śeṣebhya ekam iti

lines: Then hold high festival — four-month vow, seven days or three:
first rule or fallback. Month by month with means, or quarter-yearly, or once.
Undone, atone by murmur; the wise with means who shirk fall due —
grudged wisdom, slighted: a debt on knowing.
tsa-a20-v46.sanskrit_cite: tato mahotsavaḥ kāryaḥ cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ ca iti mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ sati vibhave māsi māsi pavitrakam atha vā caturṣu māseṣu atha vā sakṛt tadakaraṇe prāyaścittaṃ japet jñānī api sambhavadvitto 'pi akaraṇe pratyavaiti lobhopahitajñānākaraṇe jñānanindāpatteḥ

lines: When wisdom won soils the Highest's word —
then dues to pay.
tsa-a20-v47.sanskrit_cite: yadā prāpyāpi vijñānaṃ dūṣitaṃ parameśaśāsanaṃ tadā prāyaścittī

lines: So says the saying.
So ends the thread-law.
Where wisdom dawns or worldlings feast, there awareness flares high and the god-ring draws near — above all.
Weighing such heights, grant such pride of place to after-rite and the rest.
tsa-a20-v50.sanskrit_cite: jñānalābhādau laukikotsavānte 'pi sarvatra saṃvidullāsādhikyaṃ devatācakrasaṃnidhiḥ viśeṣato bhavati iti tathāvidhādhikyaparyālocanayā tathāvidham eva viśeṣam anuyāgādau kuryāt

lines: Now the forth-telling law.
Pray the all-lore master to forth-tell — he, to his own or another's, shall tell the fitting lore in fitting measure;
even the low-creed listener, for pity, his heart quickened by hope of power's fall at the Lord's wayward will — tell him, save the whispered core.
tsa-a20-v52.sanskrit_cite: sarvaśāstrasampūrṇaṃ guruṃ vyākhyārtham abhyarthayeta so 'pi svaśiṣyāya paraśiṣyāyāpi vā samucitasaṃskārocitaṃ śāstraṃ vyācakṣīta adharaśāsanasthāyāpi karuṇāvaśāt īśvarecchāvaicitryodbhāvitaśaktipātasambhāvanābhāvitahṛdayo vyācakṣīta marmopadeśavarjam

lines: Where low-seated lovers of the matter, bridled in word and mind and limb, hear telling — it bears fruit.
First, on earth anointed with scent and the rest, trace or resolve:
a lotus-ground, four-square, three lotuses, midst-lotus throned the Speech-Queen, left and right the Lord-of-Hosts and guide — adore;
on the ground-lotus, the boon-goddess of the telling.
tsa-a20-v53.sanskrit_cite: tatra nimnāsanasthitebhyaḥ tatparebhyo niyamitavāṅmanaḥkāyebhyo vyākhyā kriyamāṇā phalavatī bhavati prathamaṃ gandhādiliptāyāṃ bhuvi ullikhya saṃkalpya vā padmādhāraṃ caturaśraṃ padmatrayaṃ padmamadhye vāgīśīṃ vāmadakṣiṇayoḥ gaṇapatigurū ca pūjayet ādhārapadme vyākhyeyakalpadevatām

lines: Then sate the wheel with the common bowl-rite, then tell —
thread, sentence, chapter, unclashed fore and aft —
first wed the thesis fairly, then fairly wreck it;
prove the point, bare the drift — tell to the chapter's bound, no more;
there too, at each joint's close, sating and praise — till the telling ends.
tsa-a20-v54.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ sāmānyārghapātrayogena cakraṃ tarpayet tato vyācakṣīta sūtravākyapaṭalagrantham pūrvāparāviruddhaṃ kurvan tantrāvṛttiprasaṅgasamuccayavikalpādiśāstranyāyaucityena pūrvaṃ pakṣaṃ samyak ghaṭayitvā samyak ca dūṣayan sādhyaṃ sādhayan tātparyavṛttiṃ pradarśayan paṭalāntaṃ vyācakṣīta nādhikam tatrāpi vastvante vastvante tarpaṇaṃ pūjanam iti yāvad vyākhyāsamāptiḥ

lines: Then worshipped, dismissed the wisdom-seat, anointed —
cast it in the deep.
tsa-a20-v55.sanskrit_cite: tato 'pi pūjayitvā vidyāpīṭhaṃ visarjya upalipya agādhe tat kṣepayet

lines: So ends the telling-law.
Now the vow-clearing.
Though the truth-rooted owe no penance at all,
yet to grace the conduct-only freed, display the conduct's course.
tsa-a20-v58.sanskrit_cite: yady api tattvajñānaniṣṭhasya prāyaścittādi na kiṃcit tathāpi caryāmātrād eva mokṣabhāginaḥ tān anugrahītum ācāravartanīṃ darśayet

lines: But the truth-blind, whose heaven and release hang on conduct alone —
rule breached, no penance done — a hundred years a raw-flesh eater: so runs the penance-law.
There, she-slaying knows no penance; elsewhere, weigh strength, then unbroken Lady Garland, from once to three hundred thousand, turn and turn till doubt drops.
At the close, high worship; there too the wheel-rite — for it underlies all.
tsa-a20-v59.sanskrit_cite: atattvajñānī tu caryaikāyattabhogamokṣaḥ samayollaṅghane kṛte prāyaścittam akurvan varṣaśataṃ kravyādo bhavatīti iti prāyaścittavidhiḥ vaktavyaḥ tatra strīvadhe prāyaścittaṃ nāsti anyatra tu balābalaṃ jñātvā akhaṇḍāṃ bhagavatīṃ mālinīm ekavārāt prabhṛti trilakṣāntam āvartayet yāvat śaṅkāvicyutiḥ bhavati tadante viśeṣapūjā tatrāpi cakrayāgaḥ sa hi sarvatra śeṣabhūtaḥ

lines: So ends the vow-clearing law.
Now the master-praise law.
When all rites close and the rite is gathered in, next dawn praise the master —
first pleased as the rite's limb, not as the crown:
crown him not, and the office-bond holds you bound.
tsa-a20-v62.sanskrit_cite: sarvayāgānteṣu upasaṃhṛte yāge aparedyuḥ gurupūjāṃ kuryāt pūrvaṃ hi sa vidhyaṅgatayā toṣito na tu prādhānyena iti tāṃ prādhānyena akurvan adhikārabandhena baddho bhavati

lines: So honor it wholly.
There draw the lucky cross, there set the golden seat, there adore the whole faring-way;
by that enthrone that seat; to him worship, sating, dinner, fee, self — thus given;
beg the leavings, bow, taste yourself — then wheel-worship do.
tsa-a20-v64.sanskrit_cite: tatra svāstikaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tatra sauvarṇaṃ pīṭhaṃ dattvā tatra samastam adhvānaṃ pūjayitvā tatpīṭhaṃ tena adhiṣṭhāpya tasmai pūjāṃ kṛtvā tarpaṇaṃ bhojanaṃ dakṣiṇām ātmānam iti nivedya naivedyocchiṣṭaṃ prārthya vanditvā svayaṃ prāśya cakrapūjāṃ kuryāt

lines: So? — the master-praise law.
There — for the ripe, the rite to ripen refinement;
for the unripe, seeded freedom. Once given, the master maps life's remainder.
tsa-a20-v01.sanskrit_cite: tatra yā dīkṣā saṃskārasiddhyai jñānayogyān prati yā ca tadaśaktān prati mokṣadīkṣā sabījā tasyāṃ kṛtāyām ājīvaṃ śeṣavartanaṃ guruḥ upadiśet

lines: Daily, feastly, longed-for: threefold the leftover walk.
The last is the striver's own — here left unjudged.
tsa-a20-v02.sanskrit_cite: tatra nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyam iti trividhaṃ śeṣavartanam antyaṃ ca sādhakasyaiva tat na iha niścetavyam

lines: What returns on time is daily; to be That, the feastly;
its servants — dusk-praise, practice, feast-day, sacred thread.
tsa-a20-v03.sanskrit_cite: tatra niyatabhavaṃ nityaṃ tanmayībhāva eva naimittikaṃ tadupayogi saṃdhyopāsanaṃ pratyaham anuṣṭhānaṃ parvadinaṃ pavitrakam ityādi

lines: Even that is daily, clocked to its hour — so some.
tsa-a20-v04.sanskrit_cite: tad api nityaṃ svakālanaiyatyāt iti kecit

lines: But the feastly, though he lodge in the teaching, keeps no calendar —
master's coming, his feast, wisdom's day — so some.
tsa-a20-v05.sanskrit_cite: naimittikaṃ tu tacchāsanasthānām api aniyatam tadyathā gurutadvargāgamanaṃ tatparvadinaṃ jñānalābhadinam ityādikam iti kecit

lines: Set rite, dusk-rite, master-rite, feast-rite, the thread —
unfailing, all.
tsa-a20-v06.sanskrit_cite: tatra niyatapūjā saṃdhyopāsā gurupūjā parvapūjā pavitrakam iti avaśyaṃbhāvi

lines: Wisdom won, scripture won, the master's house neared,
birth-days, world-feasts, doctrine told, first midst and last, gods met, conclave, dream-bid, dues cleared — this feastly calls for heightened praise.
tsa-a20-v07.sanskrit_cite: naimittikam jñānalābhaḥ śāstralābho gurutadvargagṛhāgamanaṃ tadīyajanmasaṃskāraprāyaṇadināni laukikotsavaḥ śāstravyākhyā ādimadhyāntā devatādarśanaṃ melakaṃ svapnājñā samayaniṣkṛtilābhaḥ ity etat naimittikaṃ viśeṣārcanakāraṇam

lines: To the sworn, give mouth-to-mouth the chief spell —
strong, unwritten, flashing knowing's core. Then at each dusk rehearse That-ness;
through that door, at every hour, ripen such becoming; and daily adore the Highest — hearth or emblem.
tsa-a20-v08.sanskrit_cite: tatra kṛtadīkṣākasya śiṣyasya pradhānaṃ mantraṃ savīryakaṃ saṃvittisphuraṇasāram alikhitaṃ vaktrāgamenaiva arpayet tataḥ tanmayībhāvasiddhyarthaṃ sa śiṣyaḥ saṃdhyāsu tanmayībhāvābhyāsaṃ kuryāt taddvāreṇa sarvakālaṃ tathāvidhasaṃskāralābhasiddhyarthaṃ pratyahaṃ ca parameśvaraṃ ca sthaṇḍile vā liṅge vā abhyarcayet

lines: On the heart's glad hearth, glassed like stainless glass —
see your shape, no other than the worshipped ring, bodied back —
with gladdening gifts of bloom and scent, wine, drink, dish, smoke, lamp, present, hymn, song, string, drum — adore, murmur, sing — to win undoubting That-ness.
tsa-a20-v09.sanskrit_cite: tatra hṛdye sthaṇḍile vimalamakuravad dhyāte svam eva rūpaṃ yājyadevatācakrābhinnaṃ mūrtibimbitam iva dṛṣṭvā hṛdyapuṣpagandhāsavatarpaṇanaivedyadhūpadīpopahārastutigītavādyanṛttādinā pūjayet japet stuvīta tanmayībhāvam aśaṅkitaṃ labdhum

lines: Who stares unblinking at his face in glass
knows himself, and soon. No ladder leads but That-ness.
tsa-a20-v10.sanskrit_cite: ādarśe hi svamukham aviratam avalokayataḥ tatsvarūpaniścitiḥ acireṇaiva bhavet na cātra kaścit kramaḥ pradhānam ṛte tanmayībhāvāt

lines: Steeped in supreme-spell That-ness, beast-stain gone,
the whole net of bonds by devotion's taste undone — what heart abides therein is highest prize: so our masters.
tsa-a20-v11.sanskrit_cite: paramantratanmayībhāvāviṣṭasya nivṛttapaśuvāsanākalaṅkasya bhaktirasānuvedhavidrutasamastapāśajālasya yat adhivasati hṛdayaṃ tad eva paramam upādeyam iti asmadguravaḥ

lines: Couched upon it, the true-aimed
flares being's flood to light — which —
tsa-a20-v12.sanskrit_cite: adhiśayya pāramārthikaḥ bhāvaprasaraṃ prakāśam ullasati yā

lines: Supreme-deathless sight: by her they are adored —
the secret-knowers.
Ground made ready, dew-fresh with wonder's taste —
with plucked mind-blooms, self-natured, breathing their own sweet.
tsa-a20-v14.sanskrit_cite: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ

lines: From my heart's cup, brimmed with bliss-deathless, beyond price —
you, Goddess beside you, in the body's god-house — I praise by day and night.
The two-verse sense turned within — behold the god-ring.
tsa-a20-v16.sanskrit_cite: iti ślokadvayoktam artham antar bhāvayan devatācakraṃ bhāvayet

lines: Then seals shown, murmur, and the gift thereof.
Dismissal — one with what must wake.
Eat the first morsel, or drown it all —
for water's children were christened before, through the shared cake: so the lore-men.
tsa-a20-v19.sanskrit_cite: mukhyaṃ naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyāt sarvaṃ vā jale kṣipet jalajā hi prāṇinaḥ pūrvadīkṣitāḥ carubhojanadvāreṇa iti āgamavidaḥ

lines: But to feast on cat and mouse and dog breeds doubt — hellward.
Not even the wise, to bless the world, should stoop; or quit the world and sit. So ends the hearth-rite.
tsa-a20-v20.sanskrit_cite: mārjāramūṣakaśvādibhakṣaṇe tu śaṅkā janitā nirayāya iti jñānī api lokānugrahecchayā na tādṛk kuryāt lokaṃ vā parityajya āsīta iti sthaṇḍilayāgaḥ

lines: Now for the emblem: raise no sign with hidden spells —
least of all the plain. Where signs stand raised of old, in coming-and-going order, worship — the old ones bearing all.
tsa-a20-v21.sanskrit_cite: atha liṅge tatra na rahasyamantraiḥ liṅgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet viśeṣāt vyaktam iti pūrvapratiṣṭhiteṣu āvāhanavisarjanakrameṇa pūjāṃ kuryāt ādhāratayā

lines: Master's frame, your frame, Her frame, the secret book,
hero's bowl, beads, spear, arrow-gear, pearl, gold —
wrought of blooms and scents and dear stuff, or the glass — worship as the sign.
tsa-a20-v22.sanskrit_cite: tatra gurudehaṃ svadehaṃ śaktidehaṃ rahasyaśāstrapustakaṃ vīrapātram akṣasūtraṃ prāharaṇaṃ bāṇīyaṃ mauktikaṃ sauvarṇaṃ puṣpagandhadravyādihṛdyavastukṛtaṃ makuraṃ vā liṅgam arcayet

lines: By the ground's might alone spell-speed grows and grows —
the elder ground is ever chief, for spells track the ground they stand on;
and each goal crowns its own: so the book-masters.
tsa-a20-v23.sanskrit_cite: tatra ca ādhārabalād eva adhikādhikamantrasiddhiḥ bhavati iti pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ pradhānam ādhāraguṇānuvidhāyitvāt ca mantrāṇāṃ tatra tatra sādhye tattatpradhānam iti śāstraguravaḥ

lines: Everywhere, pride — no gap 'twixt me and the Highest —
alone the crowning culture.
Now the feast-law.
Common, common-common, common-rare, rare-common, rare, rarest-rare —
sixfold the feast, born of the rite's fulfillment.
tsa-a20-v26.sanskrit_cite: tatra sāmānyaṃ sāmānyasāmānyaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣo viśeṣasāmānyaṃ viśeṣo viśeṣaviśeṣaś ca iti ṣoḍhā parva

lines: Born of the rite's fulfillment.
Month by month, first and fifth are common;
fourth, eighth, ninth, fourteenth, fifteenth of either half — common-common;
on both, when due stars wed due days — common-rare.
Mārgaśīrṣa's first night-watch, dark ninth; Pauṣa's midnight, dark ninth;
Māgha's midnight, bright fifteenth; Phālguna's noon, bright twelfth;
Caitra's bright thirteenth; Vaiśākha's dark eighth; Jyaiṣṭha's dark ninth;
Āṣāḍha's first day; Śrāvaṇa's fore-noon, dark eleventh;
Bhādrapada's noon, bright sixth; Āśvayuja's bright-ninth day;
Kārttika's first night-watch, bright ninth: so the rare feast.
tsa-a20-v28.sanskrit_cite: tatra māsi māsi prathamaṃ pañcamaṃ dinaṃ sāmānyam caturthāṣṭamanavamacaturdaśapañcadaśāni dvayor api pakṣayoḥ sāmānyasāmānyam anayor ubhayor api rāśyoḥ vakṣyamāṇatattattithyucitagrahanakṣatrayoge sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ mārgaśīrṣasya prathamarātribhāgaḥ kṛṣṇanavamyām pauṣasya tu rātrimadhyaṃ kṛṣṇanavamyām māghasya rātrimadhyaṃ śuklapañcadaśyām phālgunasya dinamadhyaṃ śukladvādaśyām caitrasya śuklatrayodaśyām vaiśākhasya kṛṣṇāṣṭamyām jyaiṣṭhasya kṛṣṇanavamyām āṣāḍhasya prathame dine śrāvaṇasya divasapūrvabhāgaḥ kṛṣṇaikādaśyām bhādrapadasya dinamadhyaṃ śuklaṣaṣṭyām āśvayujasya śuklanavamīdinam kārttikasya prathamo rātribhāgaḥ śuklanavamyām iti viśeṣaparva

lines: Moon-Citrā, Jove-Maghā, Moon-Tiṣya, Witan Fore-Phalgunī,
Witan-Ear, Moon Hundred-Healers, Diti's twain,
Love-Rohiṇī, Preceptor-Branch, Moon-Ear again: so.
tsa-a20-v29.sanskrit_cite: citrācandrau maghājīvau tiṣyacandrau pūrvaphālgunībudhau śravaṇabudhau śatabhiṣakcandrau dityau rohiṇīśukrau viśākhābṛhaspatī śravaṇacandrau iti

lines: Count Mārgaśīrṣa first in due rank, skip Āśvayuja —
then rarest-rare.
tsa-a20-v30.sanskrit_cite: yadi mārgaśīrṣādikrameṇa yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bhavati āśvayujaṃ varjayitvā tadā viśeṣaviśeṣaḥ

lines: If elsewhere a rarity lights another feast —
then after-feast, say they.
tsa-a20-v31.sanskrit_cite: anyaviśeṣaś cet anyaparvaṇi tadā tat anuparva ity āhuḥ

lines: When star meets planet, the hour bows out.
The day-starved moon-day alone — by special gain; but hold the after-rite's unbroken time on feast-day chief.
By after-rite's first rank: after-rite, image-rite, wheel-rite — one name in three.
tsa-a20-v33.sanskrit_cite: tither eva viśeṣalābhāt anuyāgakālānuvṛttis tu parvadine mukhyā anuyāgaprādhānyāt parvayāgānām anuyāgo mūrtiyāgaḥ cakrayāgaḥ iti paryāyāḥ

lines: Master, his line and sons, truth-knower, maid,
outcaste, wanton, monthly-bleeder, truth-knowing dame —
in the wheel, first-honored, all as one.
tsa-a20-v34.sanskrit_cite: tatra guruḥ tadvargyaḥ sasaṃtānaḥ tattvavit kanyā antyā veśyā aruṇā tattvavedinī vā iti cakrayāge mukhyapūjyāḥ viśeṣāt sāmastyena

lines: Midmost the master, ringed in veiling order — from master down to the last bound, hero, goddess by turns —
sit ringed or ranked. Then scent and smoke and blooms in turn adore.
The bowl beheld as Ever-bliss, brimmed with Her nectar-wine;
the tasting goddess praised as Śiva; by her the god-ring sated;
the triad — man, might, Śiva — one-natured, held in mind;
then in veil-descending order, release and relish first, within, without — sate;
then circling back again: so the whole round feeds the wheel.
tsa-a20-v35.sanskrit_cite: tatra madhye guruḥ tadāvaraṇakrameṇa gurvādisamayyantaṃ vīraḥ śaktiḥ iti krameṇa ity evaṃ cakrasthityā vā paṅktisthityā vā āsīta tato gandhadhūpapuṣpādibhiḥ krameṇa pūjayet tataḥ pātraṃ sadāśivarūpaṃ dhyātvā śaktyamṛtadhyātena āsavena pūrayitvā tatra bhoktrīṃ śaktiṃ śivatayā pūjayitvā tayaiva devatācakratarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā naraśaktiśivātmakatritayamelakaṃ dhyātvā āvaraṇāvataraṇakrameṇa mokṣabhogaprādhānyaṃ bahir antaś ca tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ pratisaṃcaraṇakrameṇa evaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇaṃ cakraṃ puṣṇāti

lines: On the ground set the world-bowl; sate the ring; sate yourself with the hailed.
No bowl? Folded shell-hands, blest; or the right hand bowled — blest —
two together, right above, seamless — folded shell-hands; falling drops delight the haunters, the stream delights the Dread.
None may enter here; the strayed-in doubt not; instead redouble the wheel-rite.
Fritters and dishes scatter freely before them, as they please —
in the hidden house, nameless, all gathered under god: so the heroes' mingling-rite.
tsa-a20-v36.sanskrit_cite: tatra ādhāre viśvamayaṃ pātraṃ sthāpayitvā devatācakraṃ tarpayitvā svātmānaṃ vanditena tena tarpayet pātrābhāve bhadraṃ vellitaśuktiḥ vā dakṣahastena pātrākāraṃ bhadraṃ dvābhyām uparigatadakṣiṇābhyāṃ niḥsaṃdhīkṛtābhyām vellitaśuktiḥ patadbhiḥ bindubhiḥ vetālaguhyakāḥ saṃtuṣyanti dhārayā bhairavaḥ atra praveśo na kasyacit deyaḥ pramādāt praviṣṭasya vicāraṃ na kuryāt kṛtvā punar dviguṇaṃ cakrayāgaṃ kuryāt tato 'vadaṃśān bhojanādīn ca agre yatheṣṭaṃ vikīryeta guptagṛhe vā saṃketābhidhānavarjaṃ devatāśabdena sarvān yojayet iti vīrasaṃkarayāgaḥ

lines: At the close with gifts and leaf and cloth sate them:
so this image-rite, first of rites.
tsa-a20-v37.sanskrit_cite: tato 'nte dakṣiṇātāmbūlavastrādibhiḥ tarpayet iti pradhānatamo 'yaṃ mūrtiyāgaḥ

lines: Though no circle ever seen, the feast-days kept by image-rite
within a year bear sons'-rite fruit, no dusk-rites needed.
So for the aged, the lovers, wives — when power falls, the master teaches.
tsa-a20-v38.sanskrit_cite: adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'pi mūrtiyāgena parvadināni pūjayan varṣād eva putrakoktaṃ phalam eti vinā saṃdhyānuṣṭhānādibhiḥ iti vṛddhānāṃ bhogināṃ strīṇāṃ vidhir ayam śaktipāte sati upadeṣṭavyo guruṇā

lines: Now the thread-law.
Through Jewel-Garland, Three-Peak, Perfect Lore the thread comes law-first, crowned with the Highest's bid —
and the Light-Hall declares: threadless, all is fruitless.
tsa-a20-v40.sanskrit_cite: sa ca śrīratnamālātriśiromataśrīsiddhāmatādau vidhipūrvakaḥ pārameśvarājñāpūrakaś ca uktaṃ caitat śrītantrāloke vinā pavitrakeṇa sarvaṃ niṣphalam iti

lines: From bright Āṣāḍha to Kula-full-moon's close wear the thread;
Kārttika's dark fifteenth fills either wheel: so Night-Tantra's knowers.
tsa-a20-v41.sanskrit_cite: tatra āṣāḍhaśuklāt kulapūrṇimādināntaṃ kāryaṃ pavitrakam tatra kārttikakṛṣṇapañcadaśī kulacakraṃ nityācakraṃ pūrayati iti śrīnityātantravidaḥ

lines: Māgha's bright fifteenth: so Bhairava's Wave-knowers.
The southward sun's last fifteenth: so Sadbhāva's knowers.
Worship the god as you can afford, libate and sate, then give the thread —
wrought from gold-and-gem down to mere cloth-thread, cotton, kuśa-bellied.
tsa-a20-v44.sanskrit_cite: tatra vibhavena devaṃ pūjayitvā āhutyā tarpayitvā pavitrakaṃ dadyāt sauvarṇamuktāratnaviracitāt prabhṛti paṭasūtrakārpāsakuśagarbhāntam api kuryāt

lines: Knotted with the count of births, knotted with path-and-pitch-and-world-and-syllable-and-spell —
one to the knee, one to the navel, one to the throat, one crowned —
four threads to god and guide, brooding forms brimmed with every path; to the rest, one.
tsa-a20-v45.sanskrit_cite: tac ca tattvasaṃkhyagranthikaṃ padakalābhuvanavarṇamantrasaṃkhyagranthi ca jānvantam ekaṃ nābhyantam aparaṃ kaṇṭhāntam anyat śirasi anyat iti catvāri pavitrakāṇi devāya gurave ca samastādhvaparipūrṇatadrūpabhāvanena dadyāt śeṣebhya ekam iti

lines: Then hold high festival — four-month vow, seven days or three:
first rule or fallback. Month by month with means, or quarter-yearly, or once.
Undone, atone by murmur; the wise with means who shirk fall due —
grudged wisdom, slighted: a debt on knowing.
tsa-a20-v46.sanskrit_cite: tato mahotsavaḥ kāryaḥ cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ ca iti mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ sati vibhave māsi māsi pavitrakam atha vā caturṣu māseṣu atha vā sakṛt tadakaraṇe prāyaścittaṃ japet jñānī api sambhavadvitto 'pi akaraṇe pratyavaiti lobhopahitajñānākaraṇe jñānanindāpatteḥ

lines: When wisdom won soils the Highest's word —
then dues to pay.
tsa-a20-v47.sanskrit_cite: yadā prāpyāpi vijñānaṃ dūṣitaṃ parameśaśāsanaṃ tadā prāyaścittī

lines: So says the saying.
So ends the thread-law.
Where wisdom dawns or worldlings feast, there knowing flares high and the god-ring draws near — above all.
Weighing such heights, grant such pride of place to after-rite and the rest.
tsa-a20-v50.sanskrit_cite: jñānalābhādau laukikotsavānte 'pi sarvatra saṃvidullāsādhikyaṃ devatācakrasaṃnidhiḥ viśeṣato bhavati iti tathāvidhādhikyaparyālocanayā tathāvidham eva viśeṣam anuyāgādau kuryāt

lines: Now the forth-telling law.
Pray the all-lore master to forth-tell — he, to his own or another's, shall tell the fitting lore in fitting measure;
even the low-creed listener, for pity, his heart quickened by hope of power's fall at the Lord's wayward will — tell him, save the whispered core.
tsa-a20-v52.sanskrit_cite: sarvaśāstrasampūrṇaṃ guruṃ vyākhyārtham abhyarthayeta so 'pi svaśiṣyāya paraśiṣyāyāpi vā samucitasaṃskārocitaṃ śāstraṃ vyācakṣīta adharaśāsanasthāyāpi karuṇāvaśāt īśvarecchāvaicitryodbhāvitaśaktipātasambhāvanābhāvitahṛdayo vyācakṣīta marmopadeśavarjam

lines: Where low-seated lovers of the matter, bridled in word and mind and limb, hear telling — it bears fruit.
First, on earth anointed with scent and the rest, trace or resolve:
a lotus-ground, four-square, three lotuses, midst-lotus throned the Speech-Queen, left and right the Host-Lord and guide — adore;
on the ground-lotus, the boon-goddess of the telling.
tsa-a20-v53.sanskrit_cite: tatra nimnāsanasthitebhyaḥ tatparebhyo niyamitavāṅmanaḥkāyebhyo vyākhyā kriyamāṇā phalavatī bhavati prathamaṃ gandhādiliptāyāṃ bhuvi ullikhya saṃkalpya vā padmādhāraṃ caturaśraṃ padmatrayaṃ padmamadhye vāgīśīṃ vāmadakṣiṇayoḥ gaṇapatigurū ca pūjayet ādhārapadme vyākhyeyakalpadevatām

lines: Then sate the wheel with the common bowl-rite, then tell —
thread, sentence, chapter, unclashed fore and aft —
first wed the thesis fairly, then fairly wreck it;
prove the point, bare the drift — tell to the chapter's bound, no more;
there too, at each joint's close, sating and praise — till the telling ends.
tsa-a20-v54.sanskrit_cite: tataḥ sāmānyārghapātrayogena cakraṃ tarpayet tato vyācakṣīta sūtravākyapaṭalagrantham pūrvāparāviruddhaṃ kurvan tantrāvṛttiprasaṅgasamuccayavikalpādiśāstranyāyaucityena pūrvaṃ pakṣaṃ samyak ghaṭayitvā samyak ca dūṣayan sādhyaṃ sādhayan tātparyavṛttiṃ pradarśayan paṭalāntaṃ vyācakṣīta nādhikam tatrāpi vastvante vastvante tarpaṇaṃ pūjanam iti yāvad vyākhyāsamāptiḥ

lines: Then worshipped, dismissed the wisdom-seat, anointed —
cast it in the deep.
tsa-a20-v55.sanskrit_cite: tato 'pi pūjayitvā vidyāpīṭhaṃ visarjya upalipya agādhe tat kṣepayet

lines: So ends the telling-law.
Now the vow-clearing.
Though the truth-rooted owe no penance at all,
yet to grace the conduct-only freed, display the conduct's course.
tsa-a20-v58.sanskrit_cite: yady api tattvajñānaniṣṭhasya prāyaścittādi na kiṃcit tathāpi caryāmātrād eva mokṣabhāginaḥ tān anugrahītum ācāravartanīṃ darśayet

lines: But the truth-blind, whose heaven and release hang on conduct alone —
rule breached, no penance done — a hundred years a raw-flesh eater: so runs the penance-law.
There, she-slaying knows no penance; elsewhere, weigh strength, then unbroken Lady Garland, from once to three hundred thousand, turn and turn till doubt drops.
At the close, high worship; there too the wheel-rite — for it underlies all.
tsa-a20-v59.sanskrit_cite: atattvajñānī tu caryaikāyattabhogamokṣaḥ samayollaṅghane kṛte prāyaścittam akurvan varṣaśataṃ kravyādo bhavatīti iti prāyaścittavidhiḥ vaktavyaḥ tatra strīvadhe prāyaścittaṃ nāsti anyatra tu balābalaṃ jñātvā akhaṇḍāṃ bhagavatīṃ mālinīm ekavārāt prabhṛti trilakṣāntam āvartayet yāvat śaṅkāvicyutiḥ bhavati tadante viśeṣapūjā tatrāpi cakrayāgaḥ sa hi sarvatra śeṣabhūtaḥ

lines: So ends the vow-clearing law.
Now the master-praise law.
When all rites close and the rite is gathered in, next dawn praise the master —
first pleased as the rite's limb, not as the crown:
crown him not, and the office-bond holds you bound.
tsa-a20-v62.sanskrit_cite: sarvayāgānteṣu upasaṃhṛte yāge aparedyuḥ gurupūjāṃ kuryāt pūrvaṃ hi sa vidhyaṅgatayā toṣito na tu prādhānyena iti tāṃ prādhānyena akurvan adhikārabandhena baddho bhavati

lines: So honor it wholly.
There draw the lucky cross, there set the golden seat, there adore the whole faring-way;
by that enthrone that seat; to him worship, sating, dinner, fee, self — thus given;
beg the leavings, bow, taste yourself — then wheel-worship do.
tsa-a20-v64.sanskrit_cite: tatra svāstikaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tatra sauvarṇaṃ pīṭhaṃ dattvā tatra samastam adhvānaṃ pūjayitvā tatpīṭhaṃ tena adhiṣṭhāpya tasmai pūjāṃ kṛtvā tarpaṇaṃ bhojanaṃ dakṣiṇām ātmānam iti nivedya naivedyocchiṣṭaṃ prārthya vanditvā svayaṃ prāśya cakrapūjāṃ kuryāt

lines: So? — the master-praise law.
